AdHocCharacter.description:
``POST /stories/{id}/characters``: a character the author adds to a running story
(FR-CAT-7): #50's free-text shape — its name, its definition, its required true age
(FR-CAT-12) and optionally its safe fallback line (#68) and deflection style (FR-GUARD-7) —
and optionally ``images``, media asset ids it shows (each a live image), by reference. It is
never a player character and never a catalog entry.

examples.definition: A delivery driver in a hurry, polite and nosy.
examples.name: Dale

deflection_style.description: How the character refuses or changes the subject, in its own voice (FR-GUARD-7). Checked by the input gate.
deflection_style.title: Deflection Style

images.description: Media asset ids the character shows (images, each live), in order.
images.title: Images

AdHocCharacter.title: AdHocCharacter

AdHocPersona.description: A persona given for this story only: a persona's fields, saved nowhere.
AdHocPersona.title: AdHocPersona

AdHocSlotCharacter.description:
An ad-hoc character for an ``open`` or ``default`` role: #50's free-text shape (#114's
ad-hoc shape) — its name, its definition, its required true age (FR-CAT-12) and optionally
its safe fallback line and deflection style. Story-scoped: never a catalog entry.
AdHocSlotCharacter.title: AdHocSlotCharacter

AffectedStory.description:
One story a change affects: the capabilities it gains and loses, its backfill, whether
the upgrade is unavailable to it (it has history, and the change adds data-producing
capability), and its fingerprint before and after with the capabilities enabled and the
quality status after: those of the configuration it would run under, which is its current
one when the upgrade is unavailable (FR-PROF-16).
AffectedStory.title: AffectedStory

ApproveRequest.description:
``POST /stories/{id}/predicates/{predicate_id}/approve``: approve the whole pending
proposal (``changes`` omitted) or the fields it names.
ApproveRequest.title: ApproveRequest

Audience.description:
Who may see a reference image's subject: ``perceivable`` (only what anyone who meets the
character can see) or ``restricted`` (hidden details, a true form, the real face behind a
disguise). There is no default.
Audience.title: Audience

Backfill.description:
Whether the change needs a backfill for this story, and its estimate when it does. In M3
one is needed exactly when the upgrade is unavailable (no backfill exists until M7).
Backfill.title: Backfill

BackfillEstimate.description:
What re-deriving a story's data would take (FR-PROF-7): model calls, tokens, and the
duration in seconds with the calls made one after another.
BackfillEstimate.title: BackfillEstimate

BudgetBody.description:
The turn's model-call budget: its cap, the guardrail calls it reserved
(`guardrail_input`, `guardrail_output`) and the calls it made, which equal the entries of
`model_calls`.
BudgetBody.title: BudgetBody

BudgetOverride.description:
A request's own turn budget (NFR-PERF-6; #69), within the story's: ``max_calls`` (1 to
50, at most the story's call cap, its effective ``budgets.model_calls``) and ``deadline_s``
(seconds, at least 0.5 and at most its turn deadline, ``budgets.deadline_ms``; #113); above
either is 422 ``validation_error``.
BudgetOverride.title: BudgetOverride

CandidateBody.description:
A mention the erasure redacts only when confirmed (ADR-154): a common word of the
subject's name capitalised at the start of a sentence. The snippet is returned by the dry
run only and never stored.

candidate_id.description: Pass it in `confirm_candidates` to erase it too.
candidate_id.title: Candidate Id

field.description: The text's path in the record (dotted, list items `[n]`).
field.title: Field

snippet.description: The text around the mention, for the operator.
snippet.title: Snippet

CandidateBody.title: CandidateBody

CanonBody.description:
A canon fact about a resolved entity: its id, subject, predicate and its object (an
entity, a set or a literal), as the viewpoint may read it.
CanonBody.title: CanonBody

CardImage.description: An image on a public card (FR-CAT-4): the media asset and its alt text, nothing else.
CardImage.title: CardImage

CardRating.description:
The content rating on a public card (FR-RATE-3; #115): the rating, the version the shown
version was published under, and the rating's name.
CardRating.title: CardRating

CastSource.description: The catalog version a story character was created from.
CastSource.title: CastSource

CatalogCastCard.description:
A catalog character of the new story's cast: its public card (#115's, of the version the
story took), the story character's id, its role and its source version.
CatalogCastCard.title: CatalogCastCard

CatalogScope.description: Erase from the catalog (its characters, scenarios, personas and media).
CatalogScope.title: CatalogScope

CatalogSourceBody.description: The catalog version a story character was created from (``catalog_id@version``).
CatalogSourceBody.title: CatalogSourceBody

Caution.description: How cautious or reckless the character is.
Caution.title: Caution

CautionDisposition.description: How cautious or reckless the character is: a setting and its nuance.

nuance.description: Free text that qualifies the setting (private; at most 500 characters).
nuance.title: Nuance

CautionDisposition.title: CautionDisposition

ChainRef.description: A chain selector: the ``{turn, variant}`` of the chain's first (diverging) turn.
ChainRef.title: ChainRef

ChainRefBody.description: A chain: the ``{turn, variant}`` of its first (diverging) turn.
ChainRefBody.title: ChainRefBody

CharacterBody.description:
A character as a read returns it; ``is_player`` marks a player character. A story created
from a scenario (#119) names each character's ``role_id`` and, for a catalog character, its
``source``; a blank story's characters carry neither.
CharacterBody.title: CharacterBody

CharacterCard.description:
A catalog character's public card (``projection=card``, the default; FR-CAT-2,
FR-SCN-10): only what a player-facing client may show, never a definition field.
``version`` is the version shown; a draft read shows the draft with the latest published
version (``null`` before the first publish). ``images`` holds the primary image and the
gallery, each with its asset's alt text; ``content_rating`` is the rating's version a
published version recorded (for a draft, the rating's current version).
CharacterCard.title: CharacterCard

CharacterCardImages.description:
The card's images: the primary image (``null`` when there is none) and the gallery, in
order.
CharacterCardImages.title: CharacterCardImages

CharacterCreate.description:
``POST /catalog/characters``: the new entry's first draft (any of the draft's fields)
and, optionally, its ``owner``: an opaque principal, by default the requesting one, never
``system`` (FR-AUTH-5). Ownership confers no permission (FR-AUTH-8).

definition.personality: Patient, private and slow to trust.

public_card.name: Mara Venn
public_card.public_description: Keeps the light on Gull Rock.

definition.description: The private definition: returned only by the `full` projection.

owner.description: The entry's owner principal (default: the requesting principal; never `system`). Recorded, never interpreted.
owner.title: Owner

visual_identity.description: Optional image settings, versioned with the character.

CharacterCreate.title: CharacterCreate

CharacterDefinition.description:
The private character definition (FR-CAT-2): who the character is. It is seeded into
every story the character joins and is otherwise returned only by the ``full``
projection. ``true_age`` (FR-CAT-12) is the character's objective age, 0 to 150, never on
the card. ``deflection_style`` is how the character refuses or changes the subject: a
story's Lite prompt carries it with the character's notes, so a reply regenerated after a
guardrail violation stays in character (FR-GUARD-7). ``safe_fallback_text`` is the line the
character says when every regenerated reply fails its guardrails (#68). A definition
promoted from a story lands in ``background_flavor`` (FR-CAT-8).

deflection_style.description: How the character refuses or changes the subject, in its own voice (FR-GUARD-7; optional, private).
deflection_style.title: Deflection Style

safe_fallback_text.description: What the character says when every regenerated reply fails its guardrails (private).
safe_fallback_text.title: Safe Fallback Text

true_age.description: The character's true age (FR-CAT-12): 0 to 150. Never on the card.
true_age.title: True Age

values_motivations.description: Values and motivations, in general terms.
values_motivations.title: Values Motivations

CharacterDefinition.title: CharacterDefinition

CharacterDefinitionPatch.description:
The ``definition`` part of a draft patch: a key sets that field, ``null`` removes it,
and the groups merge the same way.
CharacterDefinitionPatch.title: CharacterDefinitionPatch

CharacterDraftBody.description:
The draft after a create or save, in ``full``: ``draft_revision`` is the revision the
next save or publish must send; ``config_revision`` is the deployment's (unchanged).
CharacterDraftBody.title: CharacterDraftBody

CharacterFull.description:
A catalog character in full (``projection=full``; FR-SCN-10): the entry's envelope, the
public card's fields with each image's media row, the aliases, the private ``definition``
and the ``visual_identity``. ``draft_revision`` is present only on a draft read
(``?draft=true``): the revision the next save or publish must send. ``published_at`` is
when ``version`` was published; ``companion_id`` names the character's companion scenario,
created with it (#116). ``owner_principal`` is the entry's owner (FR-AUTH-5), recorded
for listing and attribution only.
CharacterFull.title: CharacterFull

CharacterImageDetail.description:
An image as ``full`` shows it (FR-CAT-4; #105): the media asset's id and, from its live
row, its alt text, caption, MIME type, dimensions and generation metadata, exactly as stored
(every field ``null`` for an asset no row holds).
CharacterImageDetail.title: CharacterImageDetail

CharacterImages.description:
The public card's images (FR-CAT-4): an optional ``primary`` image and a ``gallery`` (up
to 20, distinct; the primary may also be in it), as media asset ids. The assets are
referenced, never copied: each must be a ``live`` image when it is added (422
``media_retired``), and every image is optional unless the deployment's
``require_primary_image`` is on (then a publish needs the primary).
CharacterImages.title: CharacterImages

CharacterImagesDetail.description: ``full``'s images: the primary image (``null`` when there is none) and the gallery.
CharacterImagesDetail.title: CharacterImagesDetail

CharacterImagesPatch.description:
The images part of a draft patch: ``primary`` set or removed (``null``), and ``gallery``
replaced as a whole.
CharacterImagesPatch.title: CharacterImagesPatch

CharacterListBody.description:
A page of catalog characters as cards (#110), newest first (a search: best match
first), and the cursor of the next page (``null`` on the last). No total.
CharacterListBody.title: CharacterListBody

CharacterListItem.description:
A catalog character as a listing shows it (``GET /catalog/characters``; #110): exactly
its public card (what a single read answers with ``projection=card``), plus its
``owner_principal`` (recorded for listing and attribution only, FR-AUTH-8) and when it last
changed (``updated_at``: a draft save, publish, archive, listing-status change or owner
transfer). ``rank`` is present on a search (``q``): its text-search rank, the order's first
key.
CharacterListItem.title: CharacterListItem

CharacterMetadata.description:
Search and filtering metadata, never seeded (FR-CAT-2): ``aliases`` (up to 20, each
trimmed, up to 60 characters, never the name or another alias, ignoring case), ``labels``
that describe the character (up to 30 of ``A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`` and spaces, stored trimmed and
lower-cased, distinct) and the ``content_rating_id`` (FR-RATE-3), which must be assignable
when a save sets it and is required to publish. The labels and the rating are on the card;
the aliases are searched (#110) and shown in ``full``.
CharacterMetadata.title: CharacterMetadata

CharacterMetadataPatch.description: The ``metadata`` part of a draft patch: a list replaces the stored one.
CharacterMetadataPatch.title: CharacterMetadataPatch

CharacterPatch.description:
``PATCH /catalog/characters/{id}``: a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) over the draft — a key
sets that field, ``null`` removes it, and every group merges the same way (a list replaces
the stored one) — with the ``draft_revision`` it is based on (FR-CAT-3). The draft it makes
is validated as a whole: an error is 422 at ``body.<path>``, wherever the field came from.

public_card.public_description: Keeps the light on Gull Rock, and the logbook.

draft_revision.description: The draft revision this patch is based on; a stale one is 409 `draft_stale`.
draft_revision.title: Draft Revision

CharacterPatch.title: CharacterPatch

CharacterPublicCard.description:
What a player browsing the catalog may see (FR-CAT-2): the name, a public description
(never seeded into a story) and the images.

public_description.description: Free text for the public card; never seeded into a story.
public_description.title: Public Description

CharacterPublicCard.title: CharacterPublicCard

CharacterPublicCardPatch.description: The ``public_card`` part of a draft patch.
CharacterPublicCardPatch.title: CharacterPublicCardPatch

CharacterPublishRequest.description:
``POST /catalog/characters/{id}/publish``: the character's ``draft_revision`` (FR-CAT-3)
and, when its companion's draft is published with it (``?with_companion=true``; FR-CAT-10),
the companion draft's ``companion_draft_revision``: required then, refused otherwise. A
stale revision of either is 409 ``draft_stale``.

companion_draft_revision.description: The companion draft's revision, with `with_companion=true` only (#116).
companion_draft_revision.title: Companion Draft Revision

CharacterPublishRequest.title: CharacterPublishRequest

CharacterPublishedBody.description:
The version a publish made: its number, the draft's new ``draft_revision`` (the draft
still equals what was published), the entry's ``status``, when it was published, the
validation ``report`` (no errors; its warnings and the checks this deployment cannot
run), and the ``companion`` version made with it.
CharacterPublishedBody.title: CharacterPublishedBody

CharacterSpec.description: One character of a new story's cast. ``true_age`` is required (FR-CAT-12).

deflection_style.description: How the character refuses or changes the subject, in its own voice (FR-GUARD-7): rendered with its author notes, so a reply regenerated after a guardrail violation stays in character. Checked by the input gate.
deflection_style.title: Deflection Style

CharacterSpec.title: CharacterSpec

CharacterStatusBody.description:
The entry after archive or unarchive: its status, listing status, latest published
version and when it was published, its timestamps and its companion scenario (archived and
unarchived with it; #116).
CharacterStatusBody.title: CharacterStatusBody

CharacterVersionBody.description: One published version: its number, when and by which principal it was published.
CharacterVersionBody.title: CharacterVersionBody

CharacterVersionsBody.description: Every published version of a catalog character, oldest first.
CharacterVersionsBody.title: CharacterVersionsBody

CheckProgressBody.description: How many of the history's records the check has checked, of how many.
CheckProgressBody.title: CheckProgressBody

CheckTargetBody.description: The rating the check evaluates and the version id it evaluates.
CheckTargetBody.title: CheckTargetBody

CheckViolationBody.description:
One record breaking one policy: its ``position`` (``{turn, variant, beat}``, or ``{kind,
id}`` for a seed, pinned memory, the custom instructions or an image), the policy's id and
name, and a ``code`` for a record that could not be checked. Never the text.
CheckViolationBody.title: CheckViolationBody

ClassCapabilityCounts.description: How many items fall under each field class and each capability (non-zero keys only).
ClassCapabilityCounts.title: ClassCapabilityCounts

CompanionPublishedBody.description:
The companion version a character's publish made (FR-CAT-10; #116): the companion
scenario's id, its new version (pinned to the character's new version), its draft's new
``draft_revision`` (the draft's pin moved with it; with ``with_companion`` it is what was
published) and that version's validation ``report`` (a rating difference with the character
is a ``rating_looser`` warning there).
CompanionPublishedBody.title: CompanionPublishedBody

CompanionRef.description: A character's companion scenario (#116), which follows it.
CompanionRef.title: CompanionRef

Concern.description:
One conflict between the entry and a rating: the policy (``policy_id``) or the quoted
rating-description ``clause`` it breaks (exactly one), the element, and why.
Concern.title: Concern

ConfigChangeItem.description:
One change: the revision it produced, the setting, its class, the old and new values
(secret-bearing values redacted), who made it and when.
ConfigChangeItem.title: ConfigChangeItem

ConfigChangesBody.description: A page of configuration changes, newest first, and the cursor to the next page.
ConfigChangesBody.title: ConfigChangesBody

ConfigClass.description: FR-CONC-15: how a setting's change reaches work in flight (see the module docstring).
ConfigClass.title: ConfigClass

ConfigReplacement.description:
``PUT /admin/model-config/{purpose}``: the purpose's own ``base_url``, ``model`` and
``params``, replaced in full. An omitted or ``null`` field inherits from ``default``
(``params`` per key). The API key is never part of this body (``extra=forbid``).
ConfigReplacement.title: ConfigReplacement

ContextBody.description: The assembled context within the token budget.
ContextBody.title: ContextBody

ContextItemBody.description:
A placed context item: its tier (1 ledger and pins, 2 occasions, 3 profiles and canon,
4 ranked memories), kind, id, text and tokens (``len // 4``).
ContextItemBody.title: ContextItemBody

CreatedCharacterBody.description:
A character of the new story: its id and name, and the scenario role it fills (absent
for a blank story).
CreatedCharacterBody.title: CreatedCharacterBody

CreationCounts.description:
How many errors, merge ``conflicts`` (always 0 under Lite, which detects none: FR-SCN-7)
and warnings the creation found, and what it deferred and left inactive, by field class and
capability (#122).
CreationCounts.title: CreationCounts

CreationReport.description:
What a creation from a scenario found (FR-SCN-5,6,10,11): the new story's id (``null``
when nothing was created) and its ``cast`` as cards, the ``counts``, ``unavailable`` (the
checks the deployment could not run) and, under the ``full`` projection only (``null``
under ``card``), every entry: #111's ``errors`` and ``warnings`` with their location and
exact text, every ``deferred`` item with its location and the capability it needs, and
every ``inactive`` setting.
CreationReport.title: CreationReport

CreationRules.description:
What a story creator may change at creation: ``overridable`` dotted paths (a path names
the field and everything under it), and optional ``bounds`` for settings.
CreationRules.title: CreationRules

CreationSettings.description:
The settings a story is created with: the full ``StorySettings`` schema, unknown keys
refused (M2's engine dials with the profile setting that replaced each, #113: a story
created under its profile overrides them afterwards). ``default_output_viewpoint`` names a
character of the cast **by name** here; it is stored as ``character:<id>``.

audit_retention_days.description:
How many days this story's audit records are kept before the ``retention_sweep`` deletes
them (FR-STORE-30; #71), 1 to 3650. ``None``: the deployment's ``audit_retention_days``
(default 90). Never affects story history. Prospective.
audit_retention_days.title: Audit Retention Days

default_output_viewpoint.description:
The viewpoint a read or respond falls back to when the request names none and has no
actor (FR-RESP-12): ``character:<id>``, never ``omniscient`` (#59 resolves it).
Interpretive: a Lite turn depends on it (#64).
default_output_viewpoint.title: Default Output Viewpoint

lite_summary_chunk.description: The story's override of the transcript rows per level-0 summary segment (#72).
lite_summary_chunk.title: Lite Summary Chunk

regenerate_retry_budget.description:
How many times a turn whose read set was touched is regenerated before the call fails
with ``revision_conflict`` (FR-CONC-4c). Prospective.
regenerate_retry_budget.title: Regenerate Retry Budget

turn_concurrency.description:
Same-story turn concurrency (FR-CONC-5): ``reject`` refuses an overlapping turn as busy
(423 ``story_busy``), ``queue`` queues it in a per-story FIFO (#63). Stored in its own
``stories`` column. Prospective: a change applies to requests that arrive after it.
turn_concurrency.title: Turn Concurrency

turn_queue_max.description:
How many turns may wait behind the running one under ``queue`` (``None``: the
deployment's ``turn_queue_max``, default 5); one more is 423 ``story_busy``. Stored in its
own ``stories`` column. Prospective.
turn_queue_max.title: Turn Queue Max

CreationSettings.title: CreationSettings

CurrentEntity.description: The entity the job is working on now.
CurrentEntity.title: CurrentEntity

CustomInstructionsBody.description: The story's custom instructions: standing guidance for the model, never facts.
CustomInstructionsBody.title: CustomInstructionsBody

CustomInstructionsRequest.description: The story's custom instructions, replacing the current text; ``""`` clears them.
CustomInstructionsRequest.title: CustomInstructionsRequest

CustomInstructionsWritten.description: The stored custom instructions after the edit (see ``PinnedMemoriesWritten``).
CustomInstructionsWritten.title: CustomInstructionsWritten

DeferredItem.description:
A scenario item the story cannot use yet (FR-SCN-11; a ``genesis_deferred`` row): the
dotted ``field_ref`` with indices, its class, its location (#111's shape), the one
capability it needs (a #106 module name) and its ``payload`` (``value``: the item's JSON as
the scenario holds it; ``characters``: the story character ids genesis resolved, by role).
DeferredItem.title: DeferredItem

DegradationBody.description: A degradation step and its cause (`retry_budget`, `call_budget` or `deadline`).
DegradationBody.title: DegradationBody

DepictedSubject.description:
A subject an image or video depicts (FR-IMG-9): a story ``character``, a
``catalog_character`` or a ``persona``, by id. Stored as declared, with no check that the
subject exists (it may be created later), and indexed so that erasure finds the asset
(FR-ADMIN-6).
DepictedSubject.title: DepictedSubject

Dispositions.description:
The behavioural dispositions (FR-CAT-2): five axes, each a closed five-step ``setting``
plus free-text ``nuance``. Each may be missing from a draft; a publish needs all five.
Dispositions.title: Dispositions

DispositionsPatch.description: A merge patch of the dispositions: an axis merges, ``null`` removes it.
DispositionsPatch.title: DispositionsPatch

Dominance.description: How dominant or submissive the character is.
Dominance.title: Dominance

DominanceDisposition.description: How dominant or submissive the character is: a setting and its nuance.

nuance.description: Free text that qualifies the setting (private; at most 500 characters).
nuance.title: Nuance

DominanceDisposition.title: DominanceDisposition

DormantChainBody.description:
A dormant continuation (#66): turns ``from_turn``..``through_turn`` of the chain
``{from_turn, variant}``; ``POST /stories/{id}/swap`` makes it active.
``truncate_operation_id`` names the truncation whose tail it is, when ``untruncate`` would
undo that truncation.
DormantChainBody.title: DormantChainBody

DroppedBody.description: A context item the budget left out: ``budget``, ``pin_cap`` or ``duplicate``.
DroppedBody.title: DroppedBody

EffectiveBudgetBody.description:
The budget the story's next turn plans with (#69), from its effective configuration's
`budgets` (#113): `max_model_calls_per_turn` and its `source` (`story`: the story's
overrides, `profile`: its profile's version, `deployment`: the deployment's
`profile_defaults`, or `formula`: `9 + G` when the cap is `null`), `turn_deadline` (seconds:
`budgets.deadline_ms` / 1000), the guardrail calls G it reserves (`guardrail_input`,
`guardrail_output`) and `minimum_required` (`1 + G`).
EffectiveBudgetBody.title: EffectiveBudgetBody

EffectiveConfig.description:
A story's effective configuration (FR-PROF-5,16): the deployment's defaults, the profile
and the version it runs on, its own overrides, every delivered setting at its effective
value (the defaults, then the profile's version, then the overrides), and the
configuration's fingerprint, the capabilities it enables and its quality status
(``uncertified`` in M3).

deployment_defaults.description: An engine profile's settings, by capability module (FR-PROF-2).

budgets.description: The per-turn model-call budget and deadline (NFR-PERF-6).

deadline_ms.description:
A turn's wall-clock deadline, in milliseconds (M2's ``turn_deadline``, in seconds, which
#113 moved here); the turn slot's lease and a queued request's wait follow it.
deadline_ms.title: Deadline Ms

model_calls.description:
The most model calls one turn may make, the reserved guardrail calls included (M2's
``max_model_calls_per_turn``, which #113 moved here): a cap below one generation plus those
calls refuses every turn. ``null``: NFR-PERF-6's formula (9 + the guardrail calls in M3).
model_calls.title: Model Calls

budgets.title: Budgets

hybrid_search.description: Run the lexical and exact-alias arms beside the vector arm (FR-RET-4).
hybrid_search.title: Hybrid Search

k.description: How many memories one retrieval returns.
k.title: K

recency_half_life_turns.description: The turns over which a memory's recency halves.
recency_half_life_turns.title: Recency Half Life Turns

retrieval_token_budget.description: The tokens (``len // 4``) one retrieval's assembled context may hold (FR-RET-7).
retrieval_token_budget.title: Retrieval Token Budget

weight_importance.description: The ranking's weight on decayed importance (FR-MEM-7).
weight_importance.title: Weight Importance

weight_recency.description: The ranking's weight on recency (decay over turns before the query's position).
weight_recency.title: Weight Recency

weight_similarity.description: The ranking's weight on the fused similarity of the search arms (FR-RET-5).
weight_similarity.title: Weight Similarity

hot_set.description: The hot-set budgets of the structured pipeline's memories (FR-MEM-8).
hot_set.title: HotSet

compress_threshold_tokens.description: The summary's size, in tokens, above which its segments are compressed further.
compress_threshold_tokens.title: Compress Threshold Tokens

enabled.description:
Fold messages older than the window into summary segments, and show the summary in the
prompt.
enabled.title: Enabled

window_messages.description: How many of the latest messages the prompt keeps verbatim.
window_messages.title: Window Messages

models.description: Per-purpose model routing (FR-MODEL) and the generation defaults.

generation.description: The generation defaults (FR-LITE-4): temperature, top_p and response length.
generation.title: Generation

purposes.description: Routing by purpose; a purpose left out inherits the deployment's configuration.

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$.description:
One model purpose's routing: its model and parameters; ``null`` inherits from the
deployment's model configuration (``/admin/model-config``). Endpoints and keys are never
part of a profile.

anyOf.description: Generation parameters for one purpose's calls; ``null`` inherits.
anyOf.title: RouteParams

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$.title: PurposeRoute

purposes.title: Purposes

models.title: Models

pins.description: Pinned memories (FR-LITE-3): the story's author-pinned texts, always in the prompt.

enabled.description: Include the story's pinned memories in the prompt.
enabled.title: Enabled

max_pinned.description: The most pinned memories a story may hold.
max_pinned.title: Max Pinned

pins.title: Pins

pipeline.description:
The pipeline every turn runs: ``lite`` (FR-LITE) or ``structured`` (the Engine Core
path).
pipeline.title: Pipeline

max_attempts.description: Repair attempts of the structured pipeline's repair ladder (FR-REPAIR).
max_attempts.title: Max Attempts

polish.description:
The polish pass. Under ``lite`` it is the bounded regeneration of a reply that broke an
output policy, before the safe fallback is used (FR-GUARD-6; M2's story setting
``guardrail_retry_budget``, which #113 moved here). Off, a reply that breaks a policy is
replaced by the fallback at once.

max_regenerations.description: How many times such a reply is generated again.
max_regenerations.title: Max Regenerations

polish.title: Polish

verification.description:
Claim verification, a ladder: off, declared claims only, plus claim extraction, plus
entailment escalation (FR-VERIFY); and contradiction checking (FR-PROP-10).

entailment_gate.description:
The predicate-resolution confidence below which an ``uncertain`` verdict escalates to
the entailment model (FR-VERIFY-3). The default, 1.0, escalates every one: the gate launches
conservatively and is tightened per predicate shape (#155).
entailment_gate.title: Entailment Gate

entailment_min_confidence.description:
The least confidence an entailment verdict needs to count; below it the claim takes the
safe disposition (FR-VERIFY-8).
entailment_min_confidence.title: Entailment Min Confidence

implication_max_depth.description:
How deep the bounded implication closure goes (FR-PROP-11): ``core.verify.rules`` stops
there and flags the stop in the verdict's evidence.
implication_max_depth.title: Implication Max Depth

level.description:
Raising it to ``extraction`` writes the claims extraction finds, so the ladder is
data-producing.
level.title: Level

safe_disposition.description:
What a claim the engine cannot decide becomes (FR-VERIFY-8): ``repair`` rewrites the
sentence so it no longer asserts it, and records why; ``surface`` lets the beat stand and
lists the claim in the turn report's ``uncertain_claims`` for the author.
safe_disposition.title: Safe Disposition

deleted profile (``deleted_at``) still reads and serves the stories that use it.

EntityBody.description: An entity of the story: its id, kind and canonical name.
EntityBody.title: EntityBody

EntityListRule.description:
Named entities; any whole-word mention matches, under the wordlist rules.

At story and character scope an empty ``names`` means "the story's characters": the names
are frozen into the rule when it is saved (the whole cast for a story policy, the character
itself for a character policy, #50). Every stored rule has names.
EntityListRule.title: EntityListRule

EntityProfileBody.description:
An entity's standing profile as of a turn for one viewpoint (FR-RET-6): the entity,
its relationships in both directions, its placement (``null`` when it has none the
viewpoint can read) and its inventory.
EntityProfileBody.title: EntityProfileBody

EntityType.description:
Every owned entity type (FR-AUTH-5), as ``entity_type`` columns and the registry in
``core.ownership`` name them.
EntityType.title: EntityType

Entry.description:
One finding of a validation (FR-SCN-5): its stable ``code``, its ``location``, the exact
``text`` affected (``null`` when no text is), its ``outcome`` (``rejected`` for an error), the
``source`` it names and the ``rule`` applied.

code.description: Stable and snake_case; branch on it.
code.title: Code

Entry.title: Entry

EntryLocation.description:
Where an entry points: the catalog entry, the version validated (``"draft"`` for a draft),
and when they apply the role id, the dotted field path
(``cast.roles[1].seeded_memories[0].audience``) and the seed's server-assigned id.
EntryLocation.title: EntryLocation

EntryRef.description: The entry reviewed: its type, id, and the version (``"draft"`` for the draft).
EntryRef.title: EntryRef

EntryStatus.description:
A catalog entry's version status (FR-CAT-2; #103, #108): ``draft`` until its first
publish, then ``published``; ``archived`` entries still read but cannot be edited,
published or used to create a story until they are unarchived. Postgres enum
``catalog.entry_status``.
EntryStatus.title: EntryStatus

ErasureBody.description: What the erasure did, or (``dry_run``) would do.

candidates.description: Dry run only: every candidate mention, with its id, location and a snippet. A real run lists none.
candidates.title: Candidates

candidates_remaining.description: Candidate mentions met and not confirmed, left in place (ADR-154).
candidates_remaining.title: Candidates Remaining

degradation.description: What did not complete, the erasure itself being complete: `summary_regeneration_failed`, `summary_regeneration_capped`, `rebuild_failed`. Run the erasure again to retry.
degradation.title: Degradation

media.description: Story scope: the images the subject's characters show (they stay). Catalog scope: the media assets purged, retired or rewritten.
media.title: Media

records.description: Structured rows deleted or rewritten, by table (catalog tables schema-qualified). Erasure markers and index rows are not counted.
records.title: Records

referencing_stories.description: Catalog scope: the stories that reference the subject, untouched.
referencing_stories.title: Referencing Stories

regeneration.description: `model`: rolling-summary segments that named the subject are summarised again from the redacted window; `redaction`: no model can be asked, the redacted text stands.
regeneration.title: Regeneration

residue.description: Values in the scope that still certainly name the subject after the erasure (the residue scan; 0 when nothing does). Unconfirmed candidates are not residue: `candidates_remaining` counts them.
residue.title: Residue

timeline_revision.description: Story scope: the story's revision after the erasure.
timeline_revision.title: Timeline Revision

ErasureBody.title: ErasureBody

ErasureBoundaryBody.description: What an erasure covers, what it cannot reach, and what the logs hold (FR-ADMIN-8).
ErasureBoundaryBody.title: ErasureBoundaryBody

confirm_candidates.description: Candidate mentions to erase too, by the `candidate_id` a dry run listed (ADR-154): a common word of the subject's name capitalised at the start of a sentence is erased only when confirmed here. An id the erasure does not meet is 422 `unknown_erasure_candidate`.
confirm_candidates.title: Confirm Candidates

dry_run.description: Report what would be erased and change nothing (no operation, no key).
dry_run.title: Dry Run

ErasureStatusBody.description: The erasure ledger's reconciliation: what is pending and applied, and the last run.

attempts.description: Failed reapply attempts per pending entry; retried every 5 minutes.
attempts.title: Attempts

in_progress.description: Whether a reapply is running now.
in_progress.title: In Progress

last_error.description: The last run's error, as an exception class (never a message), or null.
last_error.title: Last Error

last_run_at.description: When the last reapply run ended.
last_run_at.title: Last Run At

pending.description: Entries not applied yet, the catalog scope first, then oldest first. Each story among them is `blocked_by_erasure`: 503 `erasure_pending` until it is applied.
pending.title: Pending

ErasureStatusBody.title: ErasureStatusBody

Error.description:
The one error envelope every surface uses (docs/02 §9): REST answers it with the error's
status; the library raises the matching ``EpistrelError``.
Error.title: Error

ErrorBody.description:
What went wrong: a stable snake_case ``code``, a human ``message`` and structured
``details`` (``field`` and ``errors`` for a ``validation_error``).

code.description: Stable, snake_case; branch on it, not on the message.
code.title: Code

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody

EvaluatedRating.description: A rating the table evaluated, at the version it used (the version's id).
EvaluatedRating.title: EvaluatedRating

Feedback.description:
One principal's rating of one generated message (FR-FB-1): the message (``message_id``,
its ``turn`` and ``variant``), the ``principal``, the ``rating`` (1 to 5; null when the
principal has none), its ``tags`` and ``text``, when it was first given and last changed,
``compacted_at`` (set when an opt-in compaction removed the message; the rating is kept), the
``context`` the message was produced under (null without a rating), and the ``history`` of
earlier values, newest first.
Feedback.title: Feedback

FeedbackAggregateGroup.description:
One group: its ``key`` (null for ratings without a value in that dimension) and its
counts.
FeedbackAggregateGroup.title: FeedbackAggregateGroup

FeedbackAggregateTotals.description:
Counts over a set of ratings: how many (``count``), of how many distinct messages
(``messages``), their mean (``mean_rating``, two decimals; null with none), their
``histogram`` (keys ``1`` to ``5``), the ``tags`` they carry (present tags only) and the
``signals`` of their messages.
FeedbackAggregateTotals.title: FeedbackAggregateTotals

FeedbackAggregateWindow.description:
What the aggregate covers: ratings first given from ``from`` (inclusive) to ``to``
(exclusive; null: unbounded), and the regeneration window it used, in seconds.
FeedbackAggregateWindow.title: FeedbackAggregateWindow

FeedbackAggregates.description: ``GET /feedback/aggregates`` (FR-FB-3): the groups by one dimension, with the totals.
FeedbackAggregates.title: FeedbackAggregates

FeedbackContext.description:
The configuration a rated message was produced under, copied from its operation's
record when the rating was first written (FR-FB-1, FR-PROF-16): the operation, its
configuration fingerprint, the engine profile version (``<profile id>@<version>``), each
model purpose's model and reported version, the story's content-rating version and the
quality status. A field the operation did not record is null.
FeedbackContext.title: FeedbackContext

FeedbackExport.description:
One export's record (FR-FB-4): who exported (``principal``), when (``at``), what (the
``window``, the ``filters``, ``case_count``), its file (``bytes``, ``sha256``,
``content_url``) and its state: ``downloaded_at`` (the first download: from then on it is
delivered, outside the erasure boundary), ``expires_at`` (when the media sweep deletes the
file), ``deleted_at``/``deleted_by`` (when and by whom it was deleted; ``system`` for the
sweep) and ``redacted_at`` (when an erasure rewrote it before its download).
FeedbackExport.title: FeedbackExport

FeedbackExportFilters.description:
Which current ratings an export takes (every one by default): of one ``story_id``,
carrying any of ``tags``, rated from ``min_rating`` to ``max_rating``, of one
``config_fingerprint`` or ``profile_version`` (``<profile id>@<version>``).
FeedbackExportFilters.title: FeedbackExportFilters

FeedbackExportPage.description:
A page of the export log, newest first, and the cursor of the next page (null: the
last).
FeedbackExportPage.title: FeedbackExportPage

FeedbackExportRequest.description:
``POST /admin/feedback/export``: the window on when a rating was first given (``from``
inclusive, ``to`` exclusive; none: all time) and the ``filters``.
FeedbackExportRequest.title: FeedbackExportRequest

FeedbackExportWindow.description:
The window an export was asked for: ratings first given from ``from`` (inclusive) to
``to`` (exclusive); null is unbounded.
FeedbackExportWindow.title: FeedbackExportWindow

FeedbackExportWrittenBody.description: What the export wrote: its id, where its file is served and how many cases it holds.

content_url.description: `GET /admin/feedback/exports/{id}/content`: absolute under `public_base_url` when that is set, else the path. It needs the service credential.
content_url.title: Content Url

FeedbackExportWrittenBody.title: FeedbackExportWrittenBody

FeedbackGroupBy.description: The one dimension an aggregate groups by (see the module docstring).
FeedbackGroupBy.title: FeedbackGroupBy

FeedbackHistoryEntry.description:
An earlier value of a principal's rating of a message: the ``rating``, ``tags`` and
``text`` it held, when it was given (``rated_at``) and when it stopped being current
(``replaced_at``), because a new rating ``replaced`` it or it was ``retracted``.
FeedbackHistoryEntry.title: FeedbackHistoryEntry

FeedbackRequest.description:
``PUT /stories/{id}/messages/{message_id}/feedback``: a ``rating`` from 1 to 5, up to ten
reason ``tags`` of the deployment's ``feedback_tags`` (trimmed and lower-cased, compared as a
set; none by default; an unknown one is 422 ``unknown_feedback_tag``), and optional free
``text``, trimmed (an empty text is none) and at most the deployment's
``feedback_text_max_chars`` characters (2000 by default; 422 ``validation_error`` beyond).

examples.text: She said the same line about the tide twice.

FeedbackRequest.title: FeedbackRequest

FeedbackReviewItem.description:
One rating on a review list: the message (``story_id``, ``turn``, ``variant``,
``message_id``), the rating with its tags and text and when it was given (its latest value),
the principal who rated, the message's text and the player input it answered (null for an
opening narration), and the context the message was produced under.
FeedbackReviewItem.title: FeedbackReviewItem

FeedbackReviewPage.description:
A page of a review list, newest rating first, and the cursor of the next page (null: the
last).
FeedbackReviewPage.title: FeedbackReviewPage

FeedbackSignals.description: The implicit signals of a group's rated messages (see the module docstring).
FeedbackSignals.title: FeedbackSignals

FieldClass.description: FR-SCN-11's eight classes: where a scenario field is stored and where it may go.
FieldClass.title: FieldClass

ForkCharacterBody.description: A character of the fork and the source character it copies.
ForkCharacterBody.title: ForkCharacterBody

ForkRequest.description:
``POST /stories/{id}/fork``: copy the history through ``at_turn`` (default the head, or
the chain's tip) along ``variant_chain`` (default the active chain) into a new story.

at_turn.description: The last turn to copy (0: only the story's setup).
at_turn.title: At Turn

owner.description: The fork's owner principal (default: the requesting principal, not the source's owner; never `system`). Recorded, never interpreted.
owner.title: Owner

variant_chain.description: The chain to copy, `{turn, variant}` or `"turn:variant"` (default the active one); a dormant continuation becomes the fork's active history.

ForkRequest.title: ForkRequest

ForkedBody.description:
The new story (``timeline_revision`` is the fork's: 1), its genesis operation, where it
came from, its cast, and how many rows were copied per table.
ForkedBody.title: ForkedBody

ForkedFromBody.description:
The source story, the source revision the fork equals, the last turn copied, and the
chain followed (``null``: the active one).
ForkedFromBody.title: ForkedFromBody

GenerationMetadata.description:
How an image was generated (FR-CAT-4): the adapter, the model, the prompt and negative
prompt, the seed, the parameters (a JSON object of at most 8 KiB, every number in it finite:
``1e400``, ``NaN`` or ``Infinity`` is 422) and the ids of the reference images. Stored and
returned exactly as sent: a key that was not sent is not returned.
GenerationMetadata.title: GenerationMetadata

GenerationSettings.description:
Generation settings at one layer: deployment Lite defaults, story override, or a
request's ``prompt_params``. ``None`` inherits from the layer below.
GenerationSettings.title: GenerationSettings

GuaranteeStatus.description:
One row of the guarantee table under a configuration: the step, whether the engine
performs it by rules or a model does (``kind``), the metric that measures a model-dependent
step (an NFR-QUAL id, or ``unmeasured``; ``null`` for a deterministic step), what it needs,
and whether it is ``provided`` (``null`` for a step that runs outside stories).
GuaranteeStatus.title: GuaranteeStatus

GuaranteeTable.description:
The guarantee table of one configuration: the profile and version it reads, and every row
in ``GUARANTEES`` order (FR-VERIFY-15).
GuaranteeTable.title: GuaranteeTable

GuardrailBody.description:
The output gate's outcome: the released reply's violations (empty unless even the
last-resort fallback line broke a policy) and whether the reply is the safe fallback.
GuardrailBody.title: GuardrailBody

GuardrailCallsBody.description:
Model calls the guardrails add: ``input`` per text checked (a character-scoped input
policy adds one when its character acts), ``output`` per output checkpoint.
GuardrailCallsBody.title: GuardrailCallsBody

GuardrailViolationBody.description: An output policy the released reply breaks.
GuardrailViolationBody.title: GuardrailViolationBody

HealthChecks.description:
Each check: the database, the workers, the oldest overdue timer and job (seconds;
`null`: nothing overdue), whether ffmpeg and ffprobe (video posters and probes) are
there (`missing` never changes the status), and the erasure ledger's entries not applied
to this database yet (`erasure_pending`; above zero: `degraded`).
HealthChecks.title: HealthChecks

HealthResponse.description:
`ok`, `degraded` (still 200) or `unavailable` (503), the checks behind it, and whether

story id, at most 1,000; ``affected_count`` counts them all), the scenario recommendations
left unmet, the guarantees lost (the ids of the guarantee table's rows, FR-VERIFY-15, that

bytes), size, dimensions or duration (``null`` when no probe could read them), SHA-256
checksum, content rating and the rating's version it was uploaded under, alt text, caption,
generation metadata (as sent), source, state (``live``, or ``retired`` once deleted), the
subjects it depicts, who created it when, and, for a video, its poster's id (FR-MEDIA-3;

for the catalog scope).
PendingErasureBody.title: PendingErasureBody

Persona.description:
A saved persona (FR-CAT-6): its id, its owner (FR-AUTH-5, recorded for listing,
attribution and offboarding only), its fields, and when it was created and last changed (an
edit or an owner transfer).
Persona.title: Persona

PersonaBody.description:
The persona after a create or an edit, with the deployment's ``config_revision``
(unchanged).
PersonaBody.title: PersonaBody

PersonaCreate.description:
``POST /personas``: a persona's fields and, optionally, its ``owner``: an opaque
principal, by default the requesting one, never ``system`` (FR-AUTH-5). Ownership confers no
permission (FR-AUTH-8).

examples.description: Short-tempered and flies off the handle, but loyal to a fault. Tall, with a scar over one eyebrow.
examples.name: Sam Ortiz

description.description: Personality, and optionally appearance (up to 4,000 characters): what the player asserts they will play as. Never objective canon.
description.title: Description

owner.description: The persona's owner principal (default: the requesting principal; never `system`). Recorded, never interpreted.
owner.title: Owner

PersonaCreate.title: PersonaCreate

PersonaFields.description:
A persona's own fields (FR-CAT-6): the ``name``, an optional ``gender``, the ``age`` (its
true age, FR-CAT-12) and a short ``description`` the player asserts they will play as. The
body of an ad-hoc persona at story creation (#119) is exactly these fields.

examples.description: Short-tempered and flies off the handle, but loyal to a fault. Tall, with a scar over one eyebrow.
examples.name: Sam Ortiz

description.description: Personality, and optionally appearance (up to 4,000 characters): what the player asserts they will play as. Never objective canon.
description.title: Description

PersonaFields.title: PersonaFields

PersonaListBody.description:
A page of personas, newest first; ``next_cursor`` fetches the next page (``null`` on the
last).
PersonaListBody.title: PersonaListBody

PersonaPatch.description:
``PATCH /personas/{id}``: a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396) over the persona, last write wins.
A key sets that field, and ``null`` removes it: only ``gender`` may be removed, so ``null``
for another field is 422 at it.
PersonaPatch.title: PersonaPatch

PinnedItemBody.description: One pinned memory: its server-minted id and its text.
PinnedItemBody.title: PinnedItemBody

PinnedItemIn.description: One pinned memory in a request: an existing item's ``id`` to keep it, and its text.
PinnedItemIn.title: PinnedItemIn

PinnedMemoriesBody.description: The story's pinned memories, in prompt order.
PinnedMemoriesBody.title: PinnedMemoriesBody

PinnedMemoriesRequest.description: The story's pinned memories, in order, replacing the current set.

items.text: The bridge to the north is out.

PinnedMemoriesRequest.title: PinnedMemoriesRequest

PinnedMemoriesWritten.description:
The stored pinned memories after the edit, the edit's operation (``null`` when nothing
changed), the story's revision, and what the input gate spent (``model_calls``,
``elapsed_ms``).
PinnedMemoriesWritten.title: PinnedMemoriesWritten

PlacementBody.description:
Where the entity is: at a ``location`` (with the places that contain it, nearest
first, ``within``) or in a ``container`` (the entity holding it); the valid-time bounds and,
for ``omniscient``, the canon fact behind it.
PlacementBody.title: PlacementBody

PlannedReveal.description: A hidden truth (seeded as secret canon) with the roles allowed to learn it and when.
PlannedReveal.title: PlannedReveal

PlayerAssignment.description:
One player of a new story: the player's ``principal`` (recorded as a ``player`` relation
on the story, #119) and the ``persona`` they play as, saved or ad hoc.
PlayerAssignment.title: PlayerAssignment

PlayerInputBody.description: The actor's ``say`` and/or ``do``; at least one, and whitespace alone counts as none.
PlayerInputBody.title: PlayerInputBody

PolicyBody.description:
A policy at its current version: scope, targets, kind, effect, rule, age condition,
message and attribution.
PolicyBody.title: PolicyBody

PolicyFields.description:
``POST /admin/policies``: a global policy, or a rating policy (``scope_id`` = rating).

``id`` is a client slug or, when omitted, a new ULID.

examples.message: Do not give real-looking street addresses.
examples.name: No real addresses

PolicyFields.title: PolicyFields

PolicyKind.description:
``deterministic`` rules cost nothing; ``model_assisted`` ones cost a ``guardrail_check``
model call per check (FR-GUARD-9).
PolicyKind.title: PolicyKind

PolicyList.description: Policies, filtered as the request asked.
PolicyList.title: PolicyList

PolicyMutation.description: A policy after a write, with the deployment's ``config_revision``.
PolicyMutation.title: PolicyMutation

PolicyReplacement.description:
``PUT /admin/policies/{id}``: a full replacement. Scope and id never change, and
``applies_to`` and ``age_condition`` are required so a forgotten field cannot clear them.

examples.message: Do not give real-looking street addresses.
examples.name: No real addresses

PolicyReplacement.title: PolicyReplacement

PredicateBody.description:
A registered predicate and its semantics (FR-PROP-3): its layer (``core``, ``author``
or ``auto``), argument types, cardinality over its uniqueness key (the subject plus
``key_qualifiers``), declared qualifiers (``null``: undeclared, an auto predicate's),
temporal kind, exclusions, containment, implications, symmetry or inverse, owner and
documentation.
PredicateBody.title: PredicateBody

PredicateDecisionBody.description:
A proposal's decision: the predicate as it now is, the proposal and its status, the
fields applied, the propositions the new semantics would flag, and the story's revisions
(approval moves ``config_revision``; rejection moves nothing).
PredicateDecisionBody.title: PredicateDecisionBody

PredicateListBody.description:
The story's registry: the core vocabulary first, then the story's predicates by name;
the story's implication rules; its configuration revision.
PredicateListBody.title: PredicateListBody

PrincipalLookup.description: Every entity linked to ``principal`` (FR-AUTH-7), owned and related, by type.
PrincipalLookup.title: PrincipalLookup

ProfileAssignment.description:
``PUT /stories/{id}/engine-profile``: the profile the story runs under from its next turn
(its latest version). ``ignore_warnings`` (``ignoreWarnings``) confirms a change the impact
report warns of (FR-PROF-7).

path).
pipeline.title: Pipeline

max_attempts.title: Max Attempts

polish.description:
The polish pass. Under ``lite`` it is the bounded regeneration of a reply that broke an
output policy, before the safe fallback is used (FR-GUARD-6; M2's story setting
``guardrail_retry_budget``, which #113 moved here). Off, a reply that breaks a policy is
replaced by the fallback at once.

max_regenerations.description: How many times such a reply is generated again.
max_regenerations.title: Max Regenerations

polish.title: Polish

verification.description:
Claim verification, a ladder: off, declared claims only, plus claim extraction, plus
entailment escalation (FR-VERIFY); and contradiction checking (FR-PROP-10).

entailment_gate.description:
The predicate-resolution confidence below which an ``uncertain`` verdict escalates to
the entailment model (FR-VERIFY-3). The default, 1.0, escalates every one: the gate launches
conservatively and is tightened per predicate shape (#155).
entailment_gate.title: Entailment Gate

entailment_min_confidence.description:
The least confidence an entailment verdict needs to count; below it the claim takes the
safe disposition (FR-VERIFY-8).
entailment_min_confidence.title: Entailment Min Confidence

implication_max_depth.description:
How deep the bounded implication closure goes (FR-PROP-11): ``core.verify.rules`` stops
there and flags the stop in the verdict's evidence.
implication_max_depth.title: Implication Max Depth

level.description:
Raising it to ``extraction`` writes the claims extraction finds, so the ladder is
data-producing.
level.title: Level

safe_disposition.description:
What a claim the engine cannot decide becomes (FR-VERIFY-8): ``repair`` rewrites the
sentence so it no longer asserts it, and records why; ``surface`` lets the beat stand and
lists the claim in the turn report's ``uncertain_claims`` for the author.
safe_disposition.title: Safe Disposition

ProfileDeletedBody.description:
A deleted profile: when it was deleted, and the warnings: every story that still runs
under it (``profile_in_use``) and every scenario that recommends it
(``profile_recommended``), at most 1,000 of each; the two counts name them all. Those
stories keep running on its last version until it is purged, once no story uses it.
ProfileDeletedBody.title: ProfileDeletedBody

ProfileEditBody.description:
An edit's two stages (FR-PROF-7): ``applied``; the ``impact`` report over every story
following the profile, each with the change it sees through its own overrides; and
``result``, the profile at its latest version once the edit applied (``null`` when the
report held it back and nothing was written). ``config_revision`` is the deployment's: one
more than before when the applied edit made a new version (a configuration change every
following story runs under from its next turn, #113), unchanged otherwise.
ProfileEditBody.title: ProfileEditBody

overrides of its profile's dials (``null`` removes one), and optionally the overrides'
``expected_revision``. ``ignore_warnings`` (``ignoreWarnings``) confirms a change the impact
report warns of (FR-PROF-7).

expected_revision.description: The overrides' revision the patch was made against (0: none yet); another is 409 `revision_conflict` and nothing is written.

RespondRequest.description:
``POST /stories/{id}/respond`` and ``Engine.respond``.

- ``actor_character_id``: whose input this is. Any cast member may act, a player's own
  character or not: who acts is the consumer's call (FR-AUTH-3).
- ``player_input``: the actor's ``say``/``do``; the turn's first beat. It is only ever the
  actor's own speech and action: there is no field for another character's words, and a
  ``say`` that quotes a render character is still the actor speaking (FR-AUTH-3 b).
- ``render_character_ids``: who answers, voiced in this order in one combined reply
  (FR-RESP-5, FR-LITE-5). Omitted: every cast member except the actor, or the actor when
  no one else is in the cast. The actor may be listed. An explicit empty list is refused,
  and duplicates are dropped.
- ``output_viewpoint``: ``character:<id>`` or ``omniscient``; default the actor.
- ``prompt_params``: ``length`` (``short``/``medium``/``long`` or a token cap),
  ``temperature`` and ``top_p``, for this request only (FR-RESP-3).
- ``scene_context``: non-authoritative; never stored or placed in a prompt.
- ``budget``: this turn's ``max_calls``/``deadline_s``, within the story's (#69).
RespondRequest.title: RespondRequest

RespondResponse.description:
One finished turn: the reply, the turn's beats for the resolved viewpoint, its position,
the story's new revision, the model calls it made, where its time went, and the
configuration it ran under: ``fingerprint``, ``capabilities`` and ``quality_status``
(FR-PROF-16; null only on a replay of a turn stored before fingerprints existed), the engine
``profile`` and version it captured at its start, and the story's ``config_revision`` then
(#113, C-16; null only on a replay of a turn stored before #113).
RespondResponse.title: RespondResponse

RetrievalBody.description: What a structured render's context would retrieve for the query (FR-RET-2..7).
RetrievalBody.title: RetrievalBody

RetrievedMemoryBody.description:
One returned memory: its id, kind, text and position, its actor, occasion and
participants, its retrieval tier (``retired``: rehydrated for this query, its tier
unchanged), its importance, the arms that found it and, for a ranked memory, its score and
the terms it came from (fused similarity, recency, decayed importance).
RetrievedMemoryBody.title: RetrievedMemoryBody

ReviewedPlayerInput.description: The player input a message answered: what the acting character said and did.
ReviewedPlayerInput.title: ReviewedPlayerInput

RoleCharacter.description:

optionally, a version (omitted: the latest published when a story is created).

RoleEligibility.description:
Who may fill a role (FR-SCN-3): a character needs every label listed, one of the

RoleRelationship.description:
A relationship of the role to another role (``mother_of``, ``sibling_of``), seeded as
canon and as beliefs of the roles that know it. Free text; no inverse is added.

ScenarioCard.description:
A scenario's public card (``projection=card``, the default; FR-SCN-10): the entry's
envelope, the name, public description, media, labels and content rating, and each role's
public label and setup description with its kind and fill mode — never a world
description, seed, secret, director guidance or any other private field. ``version`` is the
version shown (a draft read shows the draft with the latest published version, ``null``
before the first publish); ``companion_of`` names the character whose companion this is
(#116).
ScenarioCard.title: ScenarioCard

ScenarioCardMedia.description:
One media asset on a scenario's card: its id, its alt text (the asset's), and its
caption (a video's caption in the scenario, else the asset's).
ScenarioCardMedia.title: ScenarioCardMedia

ScenarioCardMediaSet.description: The card's media: the cover image, the gallery images and the videos.
ScenarioCardMediaSet.title: ScenarioCardMediaSet

ScenarioCardRole.description:
A role as the card shows it: what a player choosing who fills it needs, nothing
private.
ScenarioCardRole.title: ScenarioCardRole

ScenarioCast.description:
The cast: the roles, and the most character slots (player slots included) a story
starts with (FR-SCN-4; ``null``: the deployment's default).
ScenarioCast.title: ScenarioCast

ScenarioCreate.description:
``POST /catalog/scenarios``: the new scenario's first draft — any of the draft's groups
— and, optionally, its ``owner``: an opaque principal, by default the requesting one, never
``system`` (FR-AUTH-5). Ownership confers no permission (FR-AUTH-8).

roles.setup_description: Her children are home for the weekend.
Back home for the first time in a year.

drivers.director_guidance: Keep the sale secret until the meal ends.

public_card.name: Sunday Dinner
public_card.public_description: The whole family is home for the weekend.

opening.narration: Rain on the windows; the roast is late.

world.description: A farmhouse outside a small river town.

owner.description: The scenario's owner principal (default: the requesting principal; never `system`). Recorded, never interpreted.
owner.title: Owner

ScenarioCreate.title: ScenarioCreate

ScenarioDraftBody.description:
The scenario's draft after a create or save, in ``full``: ``draft_revision`` is the
revision the next save or publish must send; ``config_revision`` is the deployment's
(unchanged).
ScenarioDraftBody.title: ScenarioDraftBody

ScenarioDrivers.description:
What drives the plot: hooks, objectives, hidden director guidance, planned reveals, and
optional milestones and endings. Instructions to the storytelling, never facts.
ScenarioDrivers.title: ScenarioDrivers

ScenarioEntity.description:
A named entity of the world (an organisation, an item, a place) with its aliases and,
optionally, its ``kind`` (#139: without one it is ``other``).
ScenarioEntity.title: ScenarioEntity

ScenarioFull.description:
A scenario in full (``projection=full``; FR-SCN-10): the entry's envelope and every field
of the document. ``draft_revision`` is present only on a draft read (``?draft=true``): the
revision the next save or publish must send. ``published_at`` is when ``version`` was
published. ``owner_principal`` is the entry's owner (FR-AUTH-5), recorded for listing and
attribution only. A companion (``companion_of``, #116) also shows ``pinned_character_version``:
the version of its character the shown version or draft is pinned to (``null`` before the
character's first publish, and for every other scenario); its locked role's
``character.version`` holds the same.
ScenarioFull.title: ScenarioFull

ScenarioListBody.description:
A page of scenarios as cards (#110), newest first (a search: best match first), and the
cursor of the next page (``null`` on the last). No total.
ScenarioListBody.title: ScenarioListBody

ScenarioListItem.description:
A scenario as a listing shows it (``GET /catalog/scenarios``; #110): exactly its public
card (what a single read answers with ``projection=card``, ``companion_of`` included), plus
its ``owner_principal`` (recorded for listing and attribution only, FR-AUTH-8) and when it
last changed (``updated_at``: a draft save, publish, archive, listing-status change or owner
transfer). ``rank`` is present on a search (``q``): its text-search rank, the order's first
key.
ScenarioListItem.title: ScenarioListItem

ScenarioLocation.description:
A named place in the world: an id roles and the opening start at, a name and a
description.
ScenarioLocation.title: ScenarioLocation

ScenarioMedia.description:
The public card's media (FR-SCN-2, FR-MEDIA-1): a cover image, gallery images and
videos, each a live media asset when it is added.
ScenarioMedia.title: ScenarioMedia

ScenarioMetadata.description:
Search and filtering metadata, returned with the card and never seeded: labels that
describe the scenario and its content rating.
ScenarioMetadata.title: ScenarioMetadata

ScenarioOpening.description:
How the story opens: the opening narration (turn 1), where it starts and which roles are
present.
ScenarioOpening.title: ScenarioOpening

ScenarioOriginBody.description: The scenario version a story was created from (#119).
ScenarioOriginBody.title: ScenarioOriginBody

ScenarioPatch.description:
``PATCH /catalog/scenarios/{id}``: a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) over the draft, group
by group — a key sets that field, ``null`` removes it, an object merges into the stored one
and an array replaces it (``roles``, ``seeded_memories``, …) — with the ``draft_revision``
it is based on (FR-CAT-3). The merged draft is validated as a whole: an invalid field is 422
at ``body.<path>``, wherever the field came from.

creation_rules.description: A JSON merge patch over the draft's `creation_rules` group (see `ScenarioCreate`): a key sets that field, `null` removes it, an object merges, an array replaces the stored one.

draft_revision.description: The draft revision this patch is based on; a stale one is 409 `draft_stale`.
draft_revision.title: Draft Revision

metadata.description: A JSON merge patch over the draft's `metadata` group (see `ScenarioCreate`): a key sets that field, `null` removes it, an object merges, an array replaces the stored one.

recommendation.description: A JSON merge patch over the draft's `recommendation` group (see `ScenarioCreate`): a key sets that field, `null` removes it, an object merges, an array replaces the stored one.
recommendation.title: Recommendation

starting_state.description: A JSON merge patch over the draft's `starting_state` group (see `ScenarioCreate`): a key sets that field, `null` removes it, an object merges, an array replaces the stored one.

story_settings_defaults.description: A JSON merge patch over the draft's `story_settings_defaults` group (see `ScenarioCreate`): a key sets that field, `null` removes it, an object merges, an array replaces the stored one.
story_settings_defaults.title: Story Settings Defaults

visual_style.description: A JSON merge patch over the draft's `visual_style` group (see `ScenarioCreate`): a key sets that field, `null` removes it, an object merges, an array replaces the stored one.

world.description: A JSON merge patch over the draft's `world` group (see `ScenarioCreate`): a key sets that field, `null` removes it, an object merges, an array replaces the stored one.

ScenarioPatch.title: ScenarioPatch

ScenarioPolicy.description:
A story-scoped guardrail policy every story from the scenario gets (FR-GUARD): a name,
the targets it applies to (default: text output), a deterministic or model-assisted rule,
an optional age condition, and the message a refusal carries. It can add to the global and
rating policies, never relax one.
ScenarioPolicy.title: ScenarioPolicy

ScenarioPublicCard.description:
What a player browsing scenarios may see: the name, a public description (never
seeded into a story) and media.
ScenarioPublicCard.title: ScenarioPublicCard

ScenarioPublishedBody.description:
The version a scenario's publish made: its number, the draft's new ``draft_revision``
(the draft still equals what was published), the scenario's ``status``, when it was
published, and the validation ``report`` (no errors; its warnings and the checks this
deployment cannot run), which the version keeps.
ScenarioPublishedBody.title: ScenarioPublishedBody

ScenarioRecommendation.description:
The engine profile and capabilities the scenario recommends (FR-PROF-7): compared with
the story's profile at creation, producing warnings, never blocks.
ScenarioRecommendation.title: ScenarioRecommendation

ScenarioRef.description:
The scenario a story is created from: its id and, optionally, a published version
(default: the latest published; any older published version may be named).
ScenarioRef.title: ScenarioRef

ScenarioRole.description:
A character role (a slot; FR-SCN-3). ``public_label`` and ``setup_description`` are
shown to the player at setup. ``kind`` is ``npc`` or ``player`` (at most one player role);
``fill`` is ``open`` (the creator picks or defines a character), ``default`` (pre-filled
with ``character``, replaceable) or ``locked`` (fixed to ``character``). A role defines
situation, not personality: whoever fills it brings their own.
ScenarioRole.title: ScenarioRole

ScenarioStartingState.description:
The story's starting state: seeded world memories, State trackers with initial values,
the starting clock, pre-scheduled events, author-declared predicates, closed sets and rules
(each stored as given in M3), and the opening.
ScenarioStartingState.title: ScenarioStartingState

ScenarioStatusBody.description:
The scenario after archive or unarchive: its status, listing status, latest published
version and when it was published, its timestamps, and the character it is the companion
of (``null`` for an authored scenario; #116).
ScenarioStatusBody.title: ScenarioStatusBody

ScenarioVersionBody.description:
One published version of a scenario: its number, when and by which principal it was
published.
ScenarioVersionBody.title: ScenarioVersionBody

ScenarioVersionsBody.description: Every published version of a scenario, oldest first.
ScenarioVersionsBody.title: ScenarioVersionsBody

ScenarioVideo.description: A video on the scenario's public card: the media asset and the caption shown with it.
ScenarioVideo.title: ScenarioVideo

ScenarioWorld.description:
The world: its description (setting and lore, seeded as canon), named locations, named
entities and, optionally, the story's own event types (#139: occasion words beyond the
engine's vocabulary, each its own word, e.g. ``joust``).
ScenarioWorld.title: ScenarioWorld

SceneBody.description:
The scene as of a turn for one viewpoint: the turn and its active variant (``null`` at
turn 0), the player character's location (``null`` when unknown to the viewpoint), and the
entities present there, characters and objects, by id.
SceneBody.title: SceneBody

SceneContext.description:
What the consumer knows about the scene (FR-RESP-4): validated, then dropped.

``characters_present`` must name cast members; in M2 it narrows nothing (M5 uses it).
SceneContext.title: SceneContext

Scope.description: Where a policy applies: the deployment, a rating, a story, or one character.
Scope.title: Scope

Seed.description:
A seeded item (FR-SCN-3,8): its ``text``, its ``holder`` (a role id, or ``world``), its
``audience`` (who starts out knowing it) and its ``disclosure`` (how the holder treats it:
``open``, ``guarded`` or ``secret``), with an optional ``kind`` (``canon``, ``belief``,
``nested`` or ``scheduled``) and ``valid_time``. ``id`` is assigned by the server when a
save stores the seed; send it back to keep it. A draft may leave the holder, audience and
disclosure out; publishing needs all three.
Seed.title: Seed

SettingTagsBody.description:
One setting's three tags: ``behavioral`` or ``data_producing`` (FR-PROF-6),
``interpretive`` or ``prospective`` (FR-CONC-15), and quality ``relevant`` or ``irrelevant``
(FR-PROF-16).
SettingTagsBody.title: SettingTagsBody

SettingsBody.description: Every deployment setting, flat, with the deployment's ``config_revision``.

profile_defaults.description: An engine profile's settings, by capability module (FR-PROF-2).

budgets.description: The per-turn model-call budget and deadline (NFR-PERF-6).

deadline_ms.description:
A turn's wall-clock deadline, in milliseconds (M2's ``turn_deadline``, in seconds, which
#113 moved here); the turn slot's lease and a queued request's wait follow it.
deadline_ms.title: Deadline Ms

model_calls.description:
The most model calls one turn may make, the reserved guardrail calls included (M2's
``max_model_calls_per_turn``, which #113 moved here): a cap below one generation plus those
calls refuses every turn. ``null``: NFR-PERF-6's formula (9 + the guardrail calls in M3).
model_calls.title: Model Calls

hybrid_search.description: Run the lexical and exact-alias arms beside the vector arm (FR-RET-4).
hybrid_search.title: Hybrid Search

k.description: How many memories one retrieval returns.
k.title: K

recency_half_life_turns.description: The turns over which a memory's recency halves.
recency_half_life_turns.title: Recency Half Life Turns

retrieval_token_budget.description: The tokens (``len // 4``) one retrieval's assembled context may hold (FR-RET-7).
retrieval_token_budget.title: Retrieval Token Budget

weight_importance.description: The ranking's weight on decayed importance (FR-MEM-7).
weight_importance.title: Weight Importance

weight_recency.description: The ranking's weight on recency (decay over turns before the query's position).
weight_recency.title: Weight Recency

weight_similarity.description: The ranking's weight on the fused similarity of the search arms (FR-RET-5).
weight_similarity.title: Weight Similarity

hot_set.description: The hot-set budgets of the structured pipeline's memories (FR-MEM-8).
hot_set.title: HotSet

compress_threshold_tokens.description: The summary's size, in tokens, above which its segments are compressed further.
compress_threshold_tokens.title: Compress Threshold Tokens

enabled.description:
Fold messages older than the window into summary segments, and show the summary in the
prompt.
enabled.title: Enabled

window_messages.description: How many of the latest messages the prompt keeps verbatim.
window_messages.title: Window Messages

generation.description: The generation defaults (FR-LITE-4): temperature, top_p and response length.
generation.title: Generation

max_pinned.title: Max Pinned

pipeline.description:
The pipeline every turn runs: ``lite`` (FR-LITE) or ``structured`` (the Engine Core
path).
pipeline.title: Pipeline

max_attempts.description: Repair attempts of the structured pipeline's repair ladder (FR-REPAIR).
max_attempts.title: Max Attempts

polish.description:
The polish pass. Under ``lite`` it is the bounded regeneration of a reply that broke an
output policy, before the safe fallback is used (FR-GUARD-6; M2's story setting
``guardrail_retry_budget``, which #113 moved here). Off, a reply that breaks a policy is
replaced by the fallback at once.

max_regenerations.description: How many times such a reply is generated again.
max_regenerations.title: Max Regenerations

polish.title: Polish

verification.description:
Claim verification, a ladder: off, declared claims only, plus claim extraction, plus
entailment escalation (FR-VERIFY); and contradiction checking (FR-PROP-10).

entailment_gate.description:
The predicate-resolution confidence below which an ``uncertain`` verdict escalates to
the entailment model (FR-VERIFY-3). The default, 1.0, escalates every one: the gate launches
conservatively and is tightened per predicate shape (#155).
entailment_gate.title: Entailment Gate

entailment_min_confidence.description:
The least confidence an entailment verdict needs to count; below it the claim takes the
safe disposition (FR-VERIFY-8).
entailment_min_confidence.title: Entailment Min Confidence

implication_max_depth.description:
How deep the bounded implication closure goes (FR-PROP-11): ``core.verify.rules`` stops
there and flags the stop in the verdict's evidence.
implication_max_depth.title: Implication Max Depth

level.description:
Raising it to ``extraction`` writes the claims extraction finds, so the ladder is
data-producing.
level.title: Level

safe_disposition.description:
What a claim the engine cannot decide becomes (FR-VERIFY-8): ``repair`` rewrites the
sentence so it no longer asserts it, and records why; ``surface`` lets the beat stand and
lists the claim in the turn report's ``uncertain_claims`` for the author.
safe_disposition.title: Safe Disposition
