SlotChoice.description:
Who fills one NPC role: a catalog character (``catalog_id`` and optionally a published
``version``; default the latest published) or an ad-hoc one (``ad_hoc``), never both.
SlotChoice.title: SlotChoice

Sources.description:
Where each effective value came from, per field (``params`` per key): ``own``, ``inherited``
(the row of the purpose this one defaults to: ``rating_suggestion`` → ``guardrail_check``)
or ``default``.
Sources.title: Sources

StageBody.description:
One stage of a long-running operation: its name, where it is, and when it got there
(null while pending).
StageBody.title: StageBody

StageStatus.description: Where one stage of a long-running operation is.
StageStatus.title: StageStatus

StatusBody.description: The story's status after an archive or unarchive, with its revision.
StatusBody.title: StatusBody

StoredResultBody.description: The stored response of the operation's ``Idempotency-Key``: its status and body.
StoredResultBody.title: StoredResultBody

StoryBody.description:
One story: the summary, its cast (true ages only for an omniscient read), its settings,
its engine profile and the version it runs on (#113; ``GET /stories/{id}/effective-config``
has the whole configuration), whether a truncation can be undone, its dormant continuations
and every variant chain.
StoryBody.title: StoryBody

StoryCharacterBody.description:
A character added to the story: its id, name and place in the cast (``ordinal``), with
the story's revision after the addition.
StoryCharacterBody.title: StoryCharacterBody

StoryCreatedBody.description:
The new story (201): its id, its cast's ids (request order for a blank story, the
scenario's role order for one created from a scenario), its rating and its revision. A
story created from a scenario (#119) also names the scenario version, the engine profile
it runs under, the creation ``report`` (counts and the unavailable checks under the
``card`` projection, every entry under ``full``) and #109's ``impact`` report. When the
impact report warns and the request did not set ``ignore_warnings`` (FR-PROF-7), nothing
is created: 200 with ``applied: false``, the reports, and no story (``story_id``,
``content_rating`` ``null``).
StoryCreatedBody.title: StoryCreatedBody

StoryFromScenario.description:
``POST /stories`` with a ``scenario`` (FR-SCN-6): the scenario (and version), who fills
each NPC role (``slots``: a ``locked`` role and a ``default`` role kept as pre-filled need
no entry; re-supplying a locked role's own ``character@version`` is accepted), each
player's principal and persona (``players``, by the scenario's player role), the
permitted ``overrides`` (dotted paths over ``story_settings_defaults``, and
``cast.max_characters_at_start``, each named by the scenario's
``creation_rules.overridable``), an optional content rating, engine profile and
starting-cast limit, ``strict`` (refuse on any creation conflict, FR-SCN-7), the story's
``name`` (default: the scenario's) and ``owner``, the report's ``projection`` (``card``:
counts; ``full``: every entry), and ``ignore_warnings`` (FR-PROF-7: create even when the
profile leaves a recommended capability unmet). ``characters`` is #50's blank-story field
and is refused beside a scenario.

ignoreWarnings.description: `ignore_warnings`, for camelCase clients (send one of the two).
ignoreWarnings.title: Ignorewarnings

ignore_warnings.description: Create even when the profile leaves a recommended capability unmet (FR-PROF-7); `ignoreWarnings` is the same flag for camelCase clients.
ignore_warnings.title: Ignore Warnings

overrides.description: Dotted paths under `story_settings_defaults` (or `cast.max_characters_at_start`) the scenario's `creation_rules.overridable` names, each with its value (validated by the scenario's field model).
overrides.title: Overrides

owner.description: The story's owner principal (default: the requesting principal; never `system`). Recorded, never interpreted.
owner.title: Owner

StoryFromScenario.title: StoryFromScenario

StoryOwnerBody.description:
A story's owner after a transfer, and its owner before. The two are equal when the request
named the current owner: nothing was recorded then. ``timeline_revision`` is the story's,
unchanged, because ownership is not story truth.
StoryOwnerBody.title: StoryOwnerBody

StoryPauseBody.description:
What pauses the story (#118): the check's job (``GET
/stories/{id}/content-rating/checks/{job_id}``), its ``cause`` (``rating_check``) and its
progress.
StoryPauseBody.title: StoryPauseBody

StoryPauseProgressBody.description: The progress of the check that paused the story: records checked, of how many.
StoryPauseProgressBody.title: StoryPauseProgressBody

StoryPolicyItem.description:
One item of a story's ``policies`` upsert list (#63's ``PATCH /stories/{id}/settings``).

A ``story`` policy's ``scope_id`` is the story; a ``character`` policy names its character.
An item with the id of an existing policy of this story edits it; any other id creates.
StoryPolicyItem.title: StoryPolicyItem

StoryProfileWriteBody.description:
An assignment's or an overrides write's two stages (FR-PROF-7): ``applied``; the
``impact`` report on the story; and ``result``, the story's effective configuration once the
change applied (``null`` when the report held it back and nothing was written). The
story's ``config_revision`` (moved by a write that changed something) and its unchanged
``timeline_revision``.
StoryProfileWriteBody.title: StoryProfileWriteBody

StoryRatingBody.description: The story's rating: the rating, its current version and its name.
StoryRatingBody.title: StoryRatingBody

done.description: How many of them have a vector in `to_version`.
done.title: Done

error.description: A failed job's exception class; never a message.
error.title: Error

StoryRelationBody.description:
The story's relation: added (201), or already there (200, nothing recorded). The
``timeline_revision`` is the story's, unchanged.
StoryRelationBody.title: StoryRelationBody

StorySettingsBody.description:
The story's settings with defaults filled in, its guardrails (effective and inactive
policies, the model calls they add) and the turn budget its next turn plans with.
StorySettingsBody.title: StorySettingsBody

StorySettingsDefaults.description:
The settings a story created from the scenario starts with (what the story is, not how
hard the engine works): each ``null`` leaves the deployment's or story's default. The
output viewpoint is a role id, which genesis turns into that role's character. Also the
story-scoped ``policies`` and the external providers the scenario requires. Unknown
setting names are refused.
StorySettingsDefaults.title: StorySettingsDefaults

StorySettingsPatch.description: A JSON merge patch (RFC 7396) over the story's settings.

audit_retention_days.description:
How many days this story's audit records are kept before the ``retention_sweep`` deletes
them (FR-STORE-30; #71), 1 to 3650. ``None``: the deployment's ``audit_retention_days``
(default 90). Never affects story history. Prospective.
audit_retention_days.title: Audit Retention Days

default_output_viewpoint.description:
The viewpoint a read or respond falls back to when the request names none and has no
actor (FR-RESP-12): ``character:<id>``, never ``omniscient`` (#59 resolves it).
Interpretive: a Lite turn depends on it (#64).
default_output_viewpoint.title: Default Output Viewpoint

lite_summary_chunk.description: The story's override of the transcript rows per level-0 summary segment (#72).
lite_summary_chunk.title: Lite Summary Chunk

policies.description: Upserts the story's own policies (never relaxing).
policies.title: Policies

regenerate_retry_budget.description:
How many times a turn whose read set was touched is regenerated before the call fails
with ``revision_conflict`` (FR-CONC-4c). Prospective.
regenerate_retry_budget.title: Regenerate Retry Budget

turn_concurrency.description:
Same-story turn concurrency (FR-CONC-5): ``reject`` refuses an overlapping turn as busy
(423 ``story_busy``), ``queue`` queues it in a per-story FIFO (#63). Stored in its own
``stories`` column. Prospective: a change applies to requests that arrive after it.
turn_concurrency.title: Turn Concurrency

turn_queue_max.description:
How many turns may wait behind the running one under ``queue`` (``None``: the
deployment's ``turn_queue_max``, default 5); one more is 423 ``story_busy``. Stored in its
own ``stories`` column. Prospective.
turn_queue_max.title: Turn Queue Max

StorySettingsPatch.title: StorySettingsPatch

StorySettingsWriteBody.description:
The settings after the write, in the read's shape, with the story's ``config_revision``
(moved by a write that changed something) and its unchanged ``timeline_revision``.
StorySettingsWriteBody.title: StorySettingsWriteBody

StorySpec.description:
``POST /stories``: a blank story with its cast, rating and settings, and optionally its
``owner`` (default: the requesting principal; never ``system``). Ownership confers no
permission (FR-AUTH-5,8).

characters.definition: An innkeeper who trusts no one.
characters.name: Ada

owner.description: The story's owner principal (default: the requesting principal; never `system`). Recorded, never interpreted.
owner.title: Owner

StorySpec.title: StorySpec

StoryStatus.description:
Where a story is in its lifecycle (#50). Stored as checked text, not a Postgres enum.

info.description:
Epistrel runs behind the consumer and must never be exposed to end users. It authenticates only the calling service, which sends one of the deployment's service credentials as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`, and it holds no user roles, grants, or permissions: which end user may call which operation, act as which character, or request which output viewpoint is the consumer's decision, made before it calls. Its privacy guarantee is relative to the request: output is produced for the output viewpoint the request names, and Epistrel does not verify that the consumer was entitled to request that viewpoint, so Epistrel by itself does not stop a player from reaching another character's secrets. Every mutating call carries an opaque requesting principal in `X-Epistrel-Principal`, which Epistrel records for attribution and never interprets; use opaque IDs rather than names or email addresses, so recorded attribution identifies no one without your own records. Ownership and relations are labels the consumer defines; the engine never grants or withholds an action because of them. Ownership exists for listing, attribution and offboarding only.

## Erasure boundary

**In scope.** An erasure removes or redacts the subject in:

- events and beats (redacted in place; each deleted record leaves an erasure marker)
- projections: transcript, story texts and heads, rebuilt from the redacted events
- rolling-summary segments (summarised again from the redacted window, or left redacted)
- pinned memories and custom instructions
- stored idempotency results
- catalog drafts and published versions, and scenario reports
- personas
- media metadata and bytes (declared subjects, captions, alt text and prompts)
- media assets that depict or name only the subject: under `erasure_shared_media = purge` (the default) the asset and its bytes are deleted; under `retire`, an asset another record still uses stays on disk, retired, with the subject removed from its metadata
- message feedback and its history
- feedback exports not yet downloaded (the subject is redacted in their cases)
- story snapshots (scenario, characters, persona) and deferred genesis items
- the story's creation report: the subject's deferred genesis items, and her cast card (see below for what a story-scope erasure keeps of a catalog character's card)
- the subject-reference index
- a backup restored after the erasure: its stories are not served until the erasure ledger, kept outside the database and copied into every backup, has been reapplied

**Out of scope.** An erasure cannot reach:

- exports already delivered
- data retained by external model/image/data providers (including hosted guardrail or image check providers)
- subjects appearing in images only visually with no declared or named reference
- backups taken before the erasure, until restored and reconciled
- logs, which never carry story content
- mentions the matcher classes as ambiguous (a name word that is also a common word, capitalised at the start of a sentence) unless the operator confirms them, and nicknames never declared as aliases; an erasure reports how many candidates remain (`candidates_remaining`). A word of the subject's name on its own is not matched when another character in the same scope also uses it (a shared surname) or when it is a title or particle (`Dr`, `de`); a common word (`will`, `rose`) is matched only capitalised. Names match in any case, fully case-folded (`Strauß` is `STRAUSS`, `Yılmaz` is `YILMAZ`), a hyphenated name by its halves at any dash, and a soft hyphen inside a word is ignored (ADR-154, ADR-155, ADR-156)
- a cast catalog character's public card in the creation report of a story she was erased from at story scope: its labels and public description stay, with its structural fields (its kind, ids, source, version and status values), while its name is redacted and its images and content rating are emptied, because the card is public catalog data, until a catalog-scope erasure of that catalog character empties it too (docs/04 C-15)

**Logs.** Operational logs contain no story content by default (NFR-SEC-4).

post.description: Right-to-be-forgotten erasure (FR-ADMIN-2, FR-ADMIN-6). `subject` is `{kind, id}` (`character`, `catalog_character` or `persona`) and `scope` `{story: <id>}` or `{catalog: true}`; a story `character` scoped to the catalog is 422 `invalid_erasure_scope`. **Story scope**: the subject's character rows, snapshots and deferred items are deleted (each leaves an erasure marker in the audit view, `include_audit=1`), every text in the story that names the subject reads `[erased]` where it did (a beat the subject said becomes `[erased]` whole, keeping its place), stored results that name it are purged, the rolling-summary segments that named it are summarised again from the redacted window (or stay redacted without a model), and the projections are rebuilt. It bumps the story's revision, so a turn in flight starts over, and runs on archived and paused stories too. **Catalog scope**: the catalog character (every version, its draft and companion) or the persona is deleted, the scenarios and other catalog records that name it are redacted, media depicting or naming only the subject are purged (or kept retired when another record still references them and `erasure_shared_media` is `retire`), and stories are never touched: `referencing_stories` lists those to erase separately. `dry_run: true` answers the counts and changes nothing (zero counts for an unknown subject). **Mentions** (ADR-154): the subject's names, aliases and name words are erased where they certainly refer to it; a name word that is also a common word (`Will`, `Rose`) only when capitalised, and at the start of a sentence it is a *candidate*: the dry run lists each one (`candidates`, with an id and a snippet returned only, never stored), and an erasure removes it only when `confirm_candidates` names its id (422 `unknown_erasure_candidate` for an id it does not meet). `candidates_remaining` counts those left. The ledger records identifiers, scope, story and counts (with the confirmed candidate ids), never content. 404 for an unknown story, or on a real run an unknown subject; 503 `config_key_missing` without `EPISTREL_CONFIG_KEY`; 503 `ledger_unavailable` when the erasure ledger's file cannot be written (nothing is erased). The erasure boundary, what erasure does not reach, is `GET /admin/erasure/boundary`.

post.description: Compare the erasure ledger's file with the database and reapply every pending erasure now (FR-ADMIN-7), as start-up and the 5-minute retry do. It answers when the run has ended; `ran` is `false` when another process was already running it, and `GET /admin/erasure/status` shows the outcome. It changes no story content of its own (each reapply is the erasure the ledger already records), takes no `Idempotency-Key` and records no operation: running it again is harmless.

parameters.description: The opaque requesting principal (FR-AUTH-4): required on every mutation (400 `principal_required` when missing, blank, longer than 256 characters, holding a control character, or the reserved `system`), recorded for attribution and never interpreted. Surrounding spaces and tabs are trimmed.
parameters.name: X-Epistrel-Principal

get.description: The erasure ledger (FR-ADMIN-7) is kept outside the database, in `EPISTREL_ERASURE_LEDGER_DIR`, and copied into the `erasure_ledger` table that every backup carries. At start-up, Epistrel compares the two: an erasure the database lacks (a restored backup that predates it) becomes pending, and its story is `blocked_by_erasure` (every read and write of it is 503 `erasure_pending`) until Epistrel has reapplied the erasure itself. This reports what is pending (with each story), how many entries are applied, whether a reapply is running, and the last run's time, error class and attempts.

post.description: Export the current ratings for the eval harness (FR-FB-4) as one JSON Lines file (`application/x-ndjson`; keys sorted, one case per line, no cases: an empty file) with one case per current rating: `position` (`{story_id, turn, variant}`), `message_id`, `player_input` (`{say, do}`, null for an opening narration), `message_text`, `rating`, `tags`, `text`, `config_fingerprint`, `profile_version`, `models` and `quality_status`. Only while the deployment's `feedback_export` setting is on (off by default): otherwise 403 `feedback_export_disabled` and nothing is written. `from` (inclusive) and `to` (exclusive) bound when a rating was first given; `filters` narrow to a `story_id`, any of `tags`, `min_rating`..`max_rating`, a `config_fingerprint` or a `profile_version`. Every variant's ratings and archived stories' are exported; a story blocked by a pending erasure is left out. The file is kept in the blob store for seven days, and every export is recorded with the exporting principal (`GET /admin/feedback/exports`). A case holds no principal, credential or setting. **Erasure boundary** (exports already delivered): Delivered exports are outside the erasure boundary (FR-ADMIN-8: exports already delivered): an export's file counts as delivered once it has been downloaded, and an erasure cannot reach a copy outside the deployment. Until its first download, an erasure redacts the subject in the file's cases.

post.description: Apply an action to everything the principal owns, chosen per type (FR-AUTH-7): `delete`, `transfer` (to `transfer_to`) or `keep` for `stories`, `characters`, `scenarios`, `personas`, `media` and `engine_profiles`, and `remove` or `keep` for the `relations` naming it on entities it does not own. A type not named is `keep`. A character's companion scenario follows the character's action. Media a transferred catalog entry references move with it, whatever the media action. Deletion uses each type's own delete: a story is deleted for every participant, catalog and persona deletion never alters stories, and media and profiles are retired. The ids are taken now, so entities created for the principal later are not included. The plan warns of stories to be deleted that others are related to, profiles to be deleted that other owners' stories use, media to be retired that other owners' records reference, and the default profile, which is never deleted. A `dry_run`, or a plan with warnings and no `ignore_warnings`, answers 200 `{applied: false, counts, warnings}` and writes nothing. Otherwise a background job carries it out, one entity at a time, resumable and safe to repeat: 202 `{job_id, counts, warnings}` with `Location`, and a retry under the same `Idempotency-Key` answers the same job. 422 `principal_reserved` for `system`, `transfer_target_required` for a `transfer` without `transfer_to`, `transfer_target_invalid` for a `transfer_to` that is the principal or `system`; 409 `offboarding_in_progress` while the principal has one queued or running. Offboarding is not erasure: the principal stays recorded on events in stories it did not own.

put.description: Change any of the deployment settings; omitted keys keep their values. Every change is recorded as a configuration change and moves `config_revision`; a write that changes nothing writes nothing. `media_moderation_webhook_url`, `public_base_url` and `max_characters_at_start_ceiling` accept `null` (unset: no hook, no base URL, no ceiling); no other key does. A list replaces the stored one. `profile_defaults` holds the engine profiles' defaults (FR-PROF-5): the bottom layer of every story's configuration, under its profile's version and its own overrides, seeded from the Lite preset. A write is laid over them (an object merges into an object; any other value replaces, `null` included, so `budgets.model_calls: null` is the formula `9 + G`), and must leave a document every profile in use and every story can run under (422 `validation_error` at the setting, or `invalid_profile` naming `details.profiles` or `details.stories`); each changed setting is recorded as `profile_defaults.<path>`. The engine dials that moved there (`lite_generation_defaults`, `lite_window_messages`, `lite_summary_max_tokens`, `max_model_calls_per_turn`) are 422 with `details.reason: superseded` and their replacement in `details.replacement`. `listing_status_values` lists the catalog's listing status values in order (a new entry takes the first; distinct, case-sensitive, 1 to 40 printable characters each); removing a value a catalog entry still holds is 409 `listing_status_in_use` (`details.value`, `details.count`). `validation_model_calls` (0 to 1000, default 0) is how many model calls one catalog validation (a publish, or a dry run) may spend on model-assisted input policies; those it does not reach are listed `unavailable` in the report. `require_primary_image` (default `false`) makes a primary image required to publish a catalog character (422 `publish_invalid`, `primary_image_required`); off, a character publishes with no image. `feedback_tags` lists the reason tags a message rating may carry (FR-FB-1's nine to start; distinct, 1 to 40 of `a-z 0-9 _` each, up to 50; may be empty); removing a tag a rating or its history still carries is 409 `feedback_tag_in_use` (`details.in_use`: each tag with its `current` and `history` counts). `feedback_text_max_chars` (1 to 20000, default 2000) caps a rating's free text, and `feedback_retention` keeps ratings for the story's life (`story_lifetime`, the default) or a number of days (1 to 3650). `rating_check_model_calls_per_record` (0 to 100, default 2) is how many model calls a rating tightening's history check may spend on one record's model-assisted policies (one it cannot afford follows its `on_uncertain`), and `rating_check_retention_days` (1 to 3650, default 30) how long a finished check is kept. `readset_change_retention_days` (1 to 3650, default 7) is how long the structured read set's change index keeps a committed change: a structured turn whose base is older conflicts instead of rebasing.

Draft revision 1, status `draft`, and the first of the deployment's `listing_status_values` (`private` by default) as its listing status. Its companion scenario (FR-CAT-5) is created with it: one NPC slot locked to the character and one player slot, the character's name and content rating and an empty world, owned and listed as the character is (`companion_id` names it). `owner` names its owner principal (default: the requesting principal; never `system`). post.description: Publish the draft as the next immutable version (FR-CAT-3): `draft_revision` is compared like a save's (409 `draft_stale`). The draft must be publishable (422 `publish_invalid` with `details.report`, every error at once): every field of the public card and the definition but the optional ones (images, background flavor, deflection style, safe fallback line; lists may be empty), each disposition axis, a true age (`true_age_missing`), a content rating that can be assigned (`content_rating_missing`, `rating_retired`), an `audience` on every reference image (`reference_image_missing_audience`), live images (`media_retired`, …) and, when the deployment's `require_primary_image` is on, a primary image (`primary_image_required`; off by default, so a character publishes with no image). The draft stays equal to what was published, at the next revision. Publishing an unchanged draft still makes a new version, and the visual identity is versioned with the rest. Warnings never block: a looser-rated character or asset (`rating_looser`), text that fails an input policy (`input_policy`), and role text that asserts personality (`personality_in_role`). The 201 answer carries the report, with the checks this deployment cannot run listed in `unavailable`, and the version keeps it. The draft stays equal to what was published, at the next revision. Publishing an unchanged draft still makes a new version. A companion scenario published alone (FR-CAT-10) is pinned to its character's latest published version, never to a character draft (`pinned_character_version`); before the character's first publish it is refused with `character_not_published`, and a rating that differs from the character's is a `rating_looser` warning.

put.description:
Replace the profile's name and settings. A new version is made only when the settings differ from the latest version's; a name-only edit makes none, and an edit that changes nothing records nothing. A preset is edited like any profile (FR-PROF-3). A deleted profile cannot be edited (422 `profile_deleted`; copy it instead). The settings may name any delivered module and level (`GET /engine-profiles/schema`); what they leave out takes the default. A shape error is 422 `validation_error` at the field; a module or level this deployment has not delivered, or a module whose dependencies are off (FR-PROF-4), is 422 `invalid_profile` naming each (`details.undelivered`, `details.missing_dependencies`), and nothing is written.

An edit runs in two stages (FR-PROF-7). Its `impact` report lists every story that follows the profile's latest version: the capabilities each gains and loses, its fingerprint before and after with the capabilities enabled and the quality status after (FR-PROF-16), whether a backfill would be needed and whether its upgrade is unavailable. The report's own `fingerprint_before`, `fingerprint_after`, `capabilities_after` and `quality_status_after` are null, since each entry states its story's, unless no story follows the profile: then they state the profile's own, before and after the edit. When the report has `warnings` and the body does not set `ignore_warnings` (`ignoreWarnings`), nothing is written and the answer is 200 with `applied: false` and the report; the `Idempotency-Key` is not kept, so the confirmation may reuse it. With `ignore_warnings`, or a report without warnings, the edit applies: `applied: true`, the report, and the profile in `result`. A data-producing increase (none is delivered in M3) cannot apply to a following story with history (a committed turn still on its timeline): that story keeps the version it ran on, and every other story moves to the new one. Each story's entry is the change it sees through its own overrides (`PATCH /stories/{id}/profile-overrides`): a setting a story overrides keeps the story's value. Settings that cannot run are refused whatever `ignore_warnings` says, and so is an edit under which a following story's overrides could not run: 422 `invalid_profile` naming those stories in `details.stories` (at most 1,000; `details.count` counts them all), with nothing written.

A new version is a configuration change (FR-PROF-6): every story that follows the profile runs under it from its next turn, and a turn already running finishes under the configuration it started with. The answer's `config_revision`, the deployment's, moves by one, and `GET /admin/config-changes` lists, at that revision, an `engine_profile:<id>` row (the old and new version numbers, with the strongest class among the changed settings) and one `engine_profile:<id>.<setting>` row per setting whose value over the deployment's `profile_defaults` changed, each with its class. A name-only edit changes no configuration and leaves `config_revision` as it is.

The rows are those of `docs/guarantees.md`, in its order, and the impact report's `guarantees_lost` names the deterministic ones a change loses by `id`. get.description: Feedback aggregates (FR-FB-3) over the current ratings, grouped by one dimension (`group_by`): `profile_version` (`<profile id>@<version>`), `fingerprint` (the configuration fingerprint), `model` (the `generation` purpose's model id), `content_rating` (the story's content rating id), `scenario` (the story's scenario id), `tag` (each reason tag; a rating counts under each of its tags, an untagged one under `null`) or `day` (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD`, when the rating was first given). All but `day` are the context the rating recorded when it was first given; a missing value is the `null` key. Each group has `count` (ratings), `messages` (distinct rated messages, the signals' denominator: the regeneration rate is `signals.regenerations / messages`), `mean_rating` (two decimals), `histogram` (keys `1` to `5`), `tags` (present tags only) and `signals`: `regenerations` of the rated messages, `regen_after_low_rating` (rated messages with a rating of 1 or 2 followed by a regeneration of the message within the deployment's `feedback_regen_window_s`, 300 s by default), `swaps_back` (swaps at the message's turn back to an older variant, untruncates included) and `rewinds` (truncates whose first discarded turn is the message). Every variant's ratings count, dormant and discarded ones too. `from` (inclusive) and `to` (exclusive) bound when a rating was first given (`from` after `to` is 422); `story_id` narrows to one story. Groups are ordered by `count`, highest first, then `key` (`null` last), at most 500 (`truncated` says when there were more); `totals` counts every rating once. Feedback is flag-only: nothing in the engine reads these reports to change a turn, a profile or a guardrail.

When the deployment configures a moderation hook, the upload (and a poster stored with it) is sent to it before anything is stored; `reject` is 422 `moderation_rejected`, and a hook that times out, cannot be reached or answers anything else is 503 `moderation_unavailable` (it fails closed). get.description: The Prometheus text exposition of the engine's metrics: identifiers and counts only, never story content (invariant 3). Served without a credential (invariant 4).

An operation's kind, status (`in_flight`, `committed`, `abandoned` or `failed`), position (`narrative_turn`, `turn_variant`), the story's `timeline_revision` once it committed, the requesting principal, its timestamps, revalidation `attempts`, `config_revisions`, `origin` (`generated` or `ingested`) and, for an ingested batch, `batch_operation_ids`. A committed Lite turn reports `queued_ms` (its wait in the story's turn queue, null when it was not queued) and `first_call_offset_ms` (from reaching the front to its first model call). A story's `genesis` operation from a scenario carries its full `creation_report` (every entry, deferred item and inactive setting) to a read with `?viewpoint=omniscient` only; otherwise it is null.

A long-running operation names what it was for in `label` and lists its `stages`, each `{name, status, at}` with `status` one of `pending`, `running`, `done`, `failed`, `skipped` (or `partial`, for an erasure's summary regeneration that rewrote only some windows) and `at` null while pending: a story's `genesis` (`validated`, `snapshotted`, `skipped` for a blank story, `materialized`); a rating change's `rating_check` or an edit's `reactivation_check` (`checking`, then `applied`/`reactivated` or `refused`); an `offboarding` (one stage per entity type, in processing order); and an `erasure` (`redacted`, `ledger_written`, `regenerated`, `rebuilt`; a catalog erasure skips the last two). Every other operation has a null `label` and no stages.

An operation that captured a read set reports `read_set`: `keys_count` (the query keys a structured turn's verdict, precondition and blocker lookups recorded, empty results included; 0 for a Lite turn), `retrieved_count` (rows read as generation context only) and, with `?viewpoint=omniscient` only, the `keys` themselves (`subject`, `predicate`, `object`, `holder`, `window`, `result_hash`); otherwise `keys` is null. `read_set` is null for an operation with no read set.

Within the idempotency result window (default 24 hours) `result` holds the stored response (`status`, `body`) of the operation's `Idempotency-Key`. A result produced for an output viewpoint (a turn) is returned only when `?viewpoint=` names that viewpoint; another named viewpoint is 409 `idempotency_conflict`. After the window `result` is absent: the operation is the reference a retry receives. Unknown ids are 404.

post.description:
Create a story, blank or from a scenario, in one operation; answers 201 with `Location`.

**Blank** (`StorySpec`): its cast (each character with a required `true_age`), its content rating (default: the deployment's) and its settings. Every character `definition` (and `deflection_style`, how it refuses or changes the subject: FR-GUARD-7) passes the input gate first: a violation is 422 `guardrail_violation` and no story exists.

**From a scenario** (`StoryFromScenario`, the body naming `scenario`; FR-SCN-6,9): the scenario (and a published version; default the latest), who fills each NPC role (`slots`: a catalog `character@version` or an `ad_hoc` definition; locked roles and default roles kept as pre-filled need none), each player's principal and persona (`players`, saved or ad hoc, in the scenario's player role), permitted `overrides`, an optional rating, engine profile and `max_characters_at_start`, and `strict`. The story is created in one transaction: one genesis operation, full snapshots of the scenario and of each catalog character (`catalog_id@version`), story settings and policies, a `player` relation per player principal, and the opening narration as turn 1. A refusal writes nothing: one 422 whose code is the first present of `creation_conflicts` (under `strict`), `slot_required`, `locked_slot_reassigned`, `player_role_fixed`, `persona_required`, `entry_archived`, `not_published`, `override_not_allowed`, `eligibility_failed`, `cast_limit_exceeded`, `rating_check_failed`, then the input gate's `guardrail_violation`, with the full creation report in `details.report`. A scenario rating mismatch is a warning (FR-RATE-5). Owners and listing statuses are never checked (FR-AUTH-8). When the engine profile leaves a capability the scenario recommends unmet, the answer is 200 with `applied: false` and the reports, unless the request sets `ignore_warnings` (FR-PROF-7).

put.description: Change the story's content rating to `content_rating_id` (FR-RATE-6,7). The two ratings are compared by their effective guardrails (live policies, inheritance included), never by their order. **Relaxing**, a target whose guardrails are a subset of the current rating's (an equal set included), applies at once with no content check: 200 `{applied: true, changed, content_rating_id, rating_version}`, recorded as the interpretive configuration change `content_rating_id` with the acting principal (`GET /stories/{id}/config-changes`). It moves the story's `config_revision`, and every operation that commits after it runs under the new rating: a turn still generating is re-checked under it before it commits. Naming the story's current rating changes nothing (`changed: false`). **Tightening**, a target that adds any policy (a sideways move included), pauses the story and checks its whole active history against the target's effective policies in the background: the player inputs and rendered beats of every active turn, generated or ingested, the pinned memories and the custom instructions. Deterministic policies run first, then model-assisted ones, outside any turn budget, within the deployment's `rating_check_model_calls_per_record`. It answers 202 `{job_id, operation_id, status: checking}` with `Location` (the check). While it runs, every call that would change the story's truth answers 409 `story_paused` with the check's progress, and reads are served. A turn already in flight commits first. If every record passes, the rating changes in one transaction and every active turn records the new guardrail set; otherwise nothing changes and the check lists each violation by position and policy. The story resumes either way. 409 `story_archived`, `story_paused` (a check already runs) or `revision_conflict`; 422 `rating_retired` for a rating that cannot be assigned.

put.description: Run the story under another engine profile, at the profile's latest version, from its next turn (FR-PROF-1,7). The story keeps its overrides; when they cannot run over the new profile the call is 422 `invalid_profile` with `details.overrides`. A profile that is deleted or unknown is 422 `profile_deleted` (`reason`). Naming the story's current profile changes nothing (200): the story keeps the version it runs on. Recorded as the setting `engine_profile_id`. Two stages (FR-PROF-7): the impact report (`impact`, one story) is always answered; a change it warns of (a capability gained or lost, an upgrade unavailable) is applied only with `ignore_warnings` (`ignoreWarnings`), and otherwise nothing is written (`applied: false`, `result: null`) and the `Idempotency-Key` is not kept, so the confirmation may reuse it. A configuration that cannot run is refused all the same (422 `invalid_profile`). Applied, `result` is the story's effective configuration after the write. The write is a story-scoped configuration change: it moves the story's `config_revision` and is listed in `GET /stories/{id}/config-changes`; the story's next turn runs under it, and a turn already running finishes under the configuration it started with. A confirmed change whose upgrade is unavailable (`upgrade_unavailable`: it adds data-producing capability to a story with history, and M3 has no backfill) keeps the story's configuration: `applied: true`, `result` is the configuration as it was, nothing is written and `config_revision` does not move. An archived story is 409 `story_archived` when the call would change something; a call that changes nothing (the story's own profile, a patch that changes no setting) answers 200 and writes nothing.

Copy the story's corrected history through `at_turn` (default the head) into a new story: every active record positioned at or before it, the cast, settings, rating, engine profile (a deleted one too: the fork runs on its last version), pinned memories, custom instructions and story policies, under new ids. The source records a `fork` event and keeps its revision. `Idempotency-Key` (per deployment, like story creation) and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` (the source's) are optional.

If they all pass, the check creates the fork and ends `reactivated` with this answer as its `outcome`; otherwise it ends `refused` with each violation and no fork is created.

Each row is one step of the guarantee boundary (FR-VERIFY-15): the model proposes; the engine validates structured claims, effects, and permissions. `kind` is `deterministic` (performed by rules) or `model_dependent` (performed by a model); a model-dependent step names the NFR-QUAL `metric` that measures it, or `unmeasured`, and a deterministic one has none (`null`). `requires` lists the modules it needs, each on at `level` or above (any level when `null`, exactly that level when `exact`), and `setting` a setting value it also needs; `purposes` names the model purposes it calls. `provided` says whether the step applies under this configuration (`null` for a step that never runs inside a story), and `delivered_in` names the milestone that delivers a step this deployment cannot provide yet. The rows are those of `docs/guarantees.md`, in its order, and the impact report's `guarantees_lost` names the deterministic ones a change loses by `id`. Only the claims detected in an output are checked.

A character viewpoint never receives `think` or `latent` beats. Under the `lite` profile perception is `none`, so every other beat is returned in full and `audience_filter` is `"none"`: Epistrel does not decide which callers may request which viewpoint. Omniscient items carry the true ages of the characters they name.

`include_audit=1` adds the turns' audit records and requires `viewpoint=omniscient` (403 `omniscient_required`). Pages hold whole turns, newest first, up to `limit` items; pass `next_before_turn` as `before_turn` for the previous page.

`variant=turn:variant` reads along another chain of the story (`GET /stories/{id}/variants`), e.g. a dormant continuation or a regenerated reply's earlier variant: the active history up to where it parts, then that chain's turns; `as_of` defaults to its tip. A chain that names no variant, or continues in more than one way, is 409 `unknown_chain`.

`include_summary=1` adds `summary`: the Lite rolling-summary segments the prompt includes now (wholly at or before `as_of`), oldest first, each `{level, covers_from, covers_to, text, operation_id}`; they are never history items.

post.description:
Record events into the story's authoritative history without generating a reply: a `player_turn` (an actor's `say`/`do`) or consumer-authored `narration` (`text`, no actor). Each event is its own narrative turn at the next turn index and advances the timeline revision; up to 50 events are recorded all or nothing, each through the input gate.

Every event carries a `client_event_id` unique within the story. Re-ingesting an ID with the same payload returns the original result and writes nothing; the same ID with a different payload is 409 `client_event_conflict`. The response is 201 when every event is new and 200 when any was replayed (`Idempotent-Replay: true` when all were). `outcome` and `state_change` events arrive in M6 (422 `unsupported_event_kind`).

patch.description: Change the story's overrides of its profile's dials (FR-PROF-5) with a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396) in `settings`: a key present sets that dial (an object merges into an object), and `null` removes the override, so the dial follows the profile again. The overrides persist across the profile's versions. A `null` must name a setting or group of the published schema (422 `validation_error` at its field; `invalid_profile` for one this deployment has not delivered). The overrides that result must be a settings document naming only delivered settings (422 `validation_error` at `body.settings.<path>`, or `invalid_profile`), and the whole configuration must run (422 `invalid_profile`); nothing is stored otherwise. They are stored without empty objects. `expected_revision` (optional) is the overrides' revision the patch was made against: another is 409 `revision_conflict` (`details.reason: overrides_revision`). A patch that changes no setting (one that removes an override the story does not have, or names an empty group) writes nothing: neither revision moves. `POST /stories/{id}/impact-preview` with the same patch in `overrides` answers this call's report without writing. Recorded as one setting per dial, `profile_overrides.<path>`. Two stages (FR-PROF-7): the impact report (`impact`, one story) is always answered; a change it warns of (a capability gained or lost, an upgrade unavailable) is applied only with `ignore_warnings` (`ignoreWarnings`), and otherwise nothing is written (`applied: false`, `result: null`) and the `Idempotency-Key` is not kept, so the confirmation may reuse it. A configuration that cannot run is refused all the same (422 `invalid_profile`). Applied, `result` is the story's effective configuration after the write. The write is a story-scoped configuration change: it moves the story's `config_revision` and is listed in `GET /stories/{id}/config-changes`; the story's next turn runs under it, and a turn already running finishes under the configuration it started with. A confirmed change whose upgrade is unavailable (`upgrade_unavailable`: it adds data-producing capability to a story with history, and M3 has no backfill) keeps the story's configuration: `applied: true`, `result` is the configuration as it was, nothing is written and `config_revision` does not move. An archived story is 409 `story_archived` when the call would change something; a call that changes nothing (the story's own profile, a patch that changes no setting) answers 200 and writes nothing.

post.description:
Play one turn of a story. The request names the acting character (any character of the story; who acts as whom is your decision), what they say and/or do (`player_input`, the turn's first beat and only ever the actor's own words), who answers (`render_character_ids`: default every other character, voiced in the order given and composed into one message), the output viewpoint (`character:<id>` or `omniscient`; default the actor, then the story's default; echoed as `output_viewpoint`, and `beats` are produced for it), prompt parameters (`length`, `temperature`, `top_p`) and optional scene context.

The consumer does no retrieval or memory work: the prompt is assembled from the story's own records. Scene context is checked against the cast and then ignored: it is never stored and never placed in the model's context.

The response is the **finished** reply: under the `lite` profile it is generated in one model call (plus one `guardrail_check` per model-assisted output policy) and none of its claims is checked against the story's facts. Before it is released the reply is checked against the story's output policies: a reply that breaks one is generated again with the policy's message as a constraint, up to the story's polish budget (its configuration's `repair.polish.max_regenerations`; none with the polish pass off), and then the character's safe fallback line is returned instead (`guardrail.fallback_used`, `degradation: ["safe_fallback"]`). Rejected drafts are audit records only. Several characters are voiced in one generation, and their knowledge is kept apart only by instructions in that shared prompt.

Every turn runs under a model-call budget and a deadline from the story's effective configuration (`GET /stories/{id}/effective-config`): `budgets.model_calls` (`null`, Lite's: `9 + G`, where G is one call per model-assisted input policy plus one per model-assisted output policy) and `budgets.deadline_ms`, or a smaller `budget: {max_calls, deadline_s}` in the request (above the story's is 422). A budget below one generation plus G is refused with 422 `budget_below_safety_minimum` (`details.minimum_required`) before any model call. The response reports `model_calls` (every attempt, failed ones included), `call_counts` by purpose, `elapsed_ms`, `budget` `{max_calls, reserved, used}` and each `degradation` step with its cause; a 503 carries `model_calls` and `elapsed_ms` in `details`. `queued_ms` is how long the turn waited in the story's turn queue (null when it never queued) and `first_call_offset_ms` the delay from the turn reaching the front (a queued turn starting, else the request arriving) to its first model call; `elapsed_ms` starts at that same moment.

The turn captures the story's configuration when it starts and runs under it to the end: the deployment's profile defaults, then the story's engine profile at its latest version, then the story's overrides (FR-PROF-5,6). The generation settings come from it, then from the request's prompt parameters (FR-LITE-4). Every response states that configuration (FR-PROF-16): the engine `profile` (`{id, version}`) and the story's `config_revision` then, its `fingerprint` (`sha256:` over the profile version, each purpose's model and every quality-relevant setting, prompt templates included), the `capabilities` it enables, and its `quality_status` (`uncertified` until a certification matches the fingerprint, which no M3 configuration can have).

Optional headers: `Idempotency-Key` (a retry returns the identical response) and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` (a stale revision is refused with 409 and nothing written).

While another turn of the story runs, a story with `turn_concurrency: reject` (the default) answers 423 `story_busy` with `Retry-After`, and one with `queue` queues the turn and plays the queued turns in order, each after the previous one finished. The request waits for its queued turn up to the story's turn deadline (`budgets.deadline_ms`), then answers 202 `{operation_id, position}` with `Location: /operations/{id}` while the turn stays queued; `Prefer: respond-async` answers 202 at once. A retry under the same `Idempotency-Key` waits for the same turn. A full queue (`turn_queue_max`) is 423.

patch.description:
Change the story's settings with a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396): a key present sets that setting and `null` resets it to its default. A story's settings describe the story: `turn_concurrency` (`reject` | `queue`), `turn_queue_max` (1-50; `null`: the deployment's default, 5), `default_output_viewpoint` (`character:<id>` of the cast, never `omniscient`), `regenerate_retry_budget` (0-10), `lite_summary_chunk` (2-200 rows per summary segment) and `audit_retention_days` (1-3650; `null`: the deployment's). An unknown key is 422. The engine's dials are the story's engine profile's, overridden per story with `PATCH /stories/{id}/profile-overrides` (FR-PROF-5): a key that moved there (`generation_settings`, `lite_window_messages`, `lite_summary_max_tokens`, `max_model_calls_per_turn`, `turn_deadline`, `guardrail_retry_budget`) is 422 with `details.reason: superseded` and the profile setting that replaced it in `details.replacement`. `policies` (optional) upserts the story's own policies; an item that would relax a policy refuses the whole request with 422 `cannot_relax` before anything is written.

Every setting but `default_output_viewpoint` is prospective: it applies to requests that arrive after the write, never to a turn already running; `default_output_viewpoint` is interpretive (a turn in flight is checked against it when it commits). A write that changes something moves the story's `config_revision`. The answer carries the budget the story's next turn plans with (`effective_budget`).

post.description:
Make the chain `to_variant_chain` (`{turn, variant}` of its first turn, as `GET /stories/{id}/variants` lists it) active: everything active after the turn where it parts from the active chain becomes `dormant`, and the chain's turns (and the work positioned on them) become `active`. Nothing is deleted; swapping back restores the exact prior state. Swapping to the active chain writes nothing (200, `operation_id` null). A chain that names no variant, or continues in more than one way, is 409 `unknown_chain` (with the `candidates` to choose from). Turns waiting in the story's queue fail with `timeline_changed`.

A control action: it bumps the story's timeline revision, and a turn generating while it commits is abandoned with 409 `timeline_changed`. `Idempotency-Key` and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` are optional.

Reactivation check (FR-RATE-7): when a turn this would make active was last checked against a guardrail set that lacks a policy now in effect (a stricter rating since it was set aside, a policy added since, or no recorded set at all), the story is paused and those turns are checked first: 202 `{job_id, operation_id, status: checking}` with `Location` (the check, `GET /stories/{id}/content-rating/checks/{job_id}`). If every turn passes, the check applies this edit and ends `reactivated` with its answer as `outcome`; otherwise it ends `refused` with each violation by position and policy, and nothing changes. Turns already checked against the current set are not checked again, and when there are none to check the edit answers synchronously as described. `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` is checked when the request is made.

post.description:
Delete a message and everything after it, without destroying anything: every operation positioned after `to_turn` becomes `discarded` (stamped with this transaction's time); no event is deleted and no valid-time changes, and `untruncate` brings them back. `to_turn` runs from 0 (keep only the story's setup) to the head - 1; anything else is 422. Turns waiting in the story's queue fail with `timeline_changed`.

A control action: it bumps the story's timeline revision, and a turn generating while it commits is abandoned with 409 `timeline_changed`. `Idempotency-Key` and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` are optional.

post.description:
Reactivate exactly what the most recent truncation discarded (undo is last in, first out). Naming `truncate_operation_id` is optional; a truncation that is not the most recent one, or none at all, is 409 `nothing_to_undo` (listing `options: ["swap", "fork"]` and the `dormant_chains` when there are any). When newer turns were written after the truncation, undoing it is a swap: the original continuation becomes active and the newer one dormant, nothing is lost, and the answer says `swapped: true` with the `active_chain`.

get.description: Every chain of the story's variant tree: each turn variant continues the active variant of the turn before it, and a chain is a run of variants continuing one another with the same membership, named by the `{turn, variant}` of its first turn. The `active` chains make up the story; `dormant` ones are continuations a swap can bring back (a regenerated reply, a rewound tail newer turns were written over); `discarded` ones are rewound tails `untruncate` can reactivate. A chain that is not active says `requires_check: true` when making it active would first check its turns against the story's current guardrails (FR-RATE-7).

parameters.description: The story's id (a ULID).
parameters.name: story_id

tags.description: Catalog characters and scenarios: drafts, immutable published versions and their `card`/`full` projections (FR-CAT, FR-SCN-1..4,10).
tags.name: catalog

tags.description: Media assets: immutable, content-addressed images and videos with their declared depicted subjects, an optional moderation hook, and delete-as-retire (FR-MEDIA-1,2); byte ranges, short-lived signed URLs, resumable uploads and a poster for every video (FR-MEDIA-3).
tags.name: media

tags.description: Engine profiles: named, versioned sets of capability modules and dials that set how hard the engine works for a story (FR-PROF-1..4). The schema exposes only the modules and levels this deployment has delivered; presets are ordinary profiles. A story runs under its profile's latest version with its own overrides over it, on top of the deployment's defaults (FR-PROF-5,6).
tags.name: profiles

tags.description: Player personas (FR-CAT-6): the name, gender, age and short description a player plays as, saved per principal for reuse. A persona is not a catalog entry, and a story keeps a snapshot of the one it was created with, so editing or deleting a persona never changes a story.
tags.name: personas

tags.description: Principal lookup (FR-AUTH-7): everything linked to a principal, owned and related, by type, with counts and pages. Principals are opaque and never resolved; offboarding is under `/admin/offboarding`.
tags.name: principals

tags.description: Each owned entity's one owner and its relations (FR-AUTH-5,6): transfers and relation changes, recorded with the acting principal. Ownership and relations exist for listing, attribution and offboarding only; nothing gates on them (FR-AUTH-8).
tags.name: ownership

tags.description: Message feedback: each principal's rating (1 to 5) of a generated message, with reason tags and free text, recorded with the configuration the message was produced under (FR-FB-1). Feedback is an audit record: nothing in the story reads it, and it changes no engine behavior (FR-FB-2). Its aggregates with the implicit signals, the guardrail and memory review lists (FR-FB-3), and the operator's opt-in export of labelled cases under `/admin/feedback` (FR-FB-4) are flag-only reports.
tags.name: feedback
